And in another hand: I, Bishop Emeritus, have reviewed it.

87. Marcellinus, most illustrious man, tribune and notary, said: Your eminence’s statement expressly maintains that those present received mandates from those present, since all who subscribed can readily be recognized by you [Col. 1278D] and by all your people. Therefore, when the subscriptions have been read in order, whoever is doubted may come immediately.

88. Bishop Adeodatus said: I offer the opposing party an expedient, lest they think disorder may occur when both parties are present. Let our fellow bishops assemble in one place, and let them cause their own men to come to another place. When all the locations have been read aloud, let two men be sent, so that every ground of dispute and every disturbance may be removed. And in another hand: I, Bishop Adeodatus, have reviewed it.

89. Alypius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: A novel demand is now being made by the opposing party. For we, obedient to the commands of the edict, came in the number [Col. 1279A] defined by the edict. But since concern for those present must not be refused even in this matter—although inquiry into the number is not part of our present proceeding—order that such of our brethren as can now be found present be admitted. If any happen to be absent, their presence will be shown to your own eyes tomorrow; provided only that no delay in the case arise. Since we are present in a definite number, chosen by the universal Catholic council, let these same men, now confirmed to assert the case, undertake the whole burden of it, so that no delay can be raised against the question. And in another hand: I have reviewed it.

90. Bishop Adeodatus said: Order that the mandate of these same men, where they subscribed, be shown to us—the mandate just now read by the official staff. And in another hand: I, Bishop Adeodatus, [Col. 1279B] have reviewed it.

91. Marcellinus, most illustrious man, tribune and notary, said: Let the mandate just now read by the official staff, in which the subscriptions of all are contained, be shown to those requesting it.

92. Bishop Petilianus said: This inconsistency causes us great concern. Either let them today produce the number of those whom they say commissioned them to act, or they themselves have postponed the case until tomorrow. And in another hand: I, Bishop Petilianus, have reviewed it.

93. Alypius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: The case has not been postponed; it is to be conducted today. And in another hand: I have reviewed it. Bishop Augustine said: Let the mandate be offered into the proceedings; let it be offered by the official staff.

94. Bishop Adeodatus said: This is what we expected; [Col. 1279C] this is what we desired: that the same proceedings to which they subscribed should now be present until those who gave the mandate come. And in another hand: I, Bishop Adeodatus, have reviewed it.

95. Marcellinus, most illustrious man, tribune and notary, said: This must be done in such a way that, if you entertain any concern, the documents sealed by you may be preserved.

96. Bishop Petilianus said: We require their presence, not the mandate. And in another hand: I, Bishop Petilianus, have reviewed it.

97. Fortunatianus, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: We have already requested that our brethren and fellow priests who can be found present should be admitted. Let your nobility order the superfluous knot of the dispute cut away, so that, once admitted, they may at least furnish due assurance to their eyes. And in another hand: I have reviewed it.

[Col. 1279D] 98. Marcellinus, most illustrious man, tribune and notary, said: Let these venerable priests who are said to be present deign to come. And the Catholic bishops entered.

Marcellinus, most illustrious man, tribune and notary, said: “I recognize that your entire request has been satisfied.” And he added: “The bishops whom you wished to enter are present; they are known to have selected, in accordance with the form of the imperial command and the tenor of the edict, a fixed number for conducting the case. Therefore, so that there may hereafter be no doubt or perhaps confusion, [Col. 1280A] let the individual subscriptions be read aloud, so that, once they have been identified, they may be pleased to withdraw.”

99. Martialis, recorder, read out by command: “Aurelius, bishop of the Catholic Church of Carthage, residing at Carthage: in the presence of Marcellinus, most illustrious man, tribune and notary, I received and subscribed this authorization.” All the rest subscribed in this manner. He then read: “Silvanus, bishop of the Catholic Church of Summa.” He said: “I am present.” Marcellinus, most illustrious man, tribune and notary, said: “Let Silvanus, who did not accept the conference, withdraw.” After he had withdrawn, the same man read: “Valentinus, bishop of the Church of Vaia.” [Note: [Col. 1279D] Valentinus of Vaia. He was primate of Numidia in 419, when he attended the Council of Carthage.] He said: “I am present.”

100. Alypius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “They have made us anxious; they themselves first impressed upon us the need for diligence. As our people are named, so we also have doubts concerning their number.” And in another hand: “I have acknowledged it.”

101. Marcellinus, most illustrious man, tribune and notary, said: “So it shall be done; yet the opposing party agrees that, once they have been identified together, they shall withdraw.”

102. Aurelius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “But first they too must give authorization, so that it may appear that they are here.” And in another hand: “I have acknowledged it.”

103. Marcellinus, most illustrious man, tribune and notary, said: “Then does it please Your Holiness that, after the authorization has been completed, the venerable men, bishops of your party as well, withdraw; that the case be conducted among a few; and that you may deign to answer what has been asked?”

104. Primianus, bishop of the Church of Carthage, [Col. 1280C] said: “Since we too have given authorization in the records as persons present, we withdraw and yield the place to the parties to the suit; nevertheless, we shall be close at hand.” And in another hand: “I, Primianus the bishop, have acknowledged it.”

105. Marcellinus, most illustrious man, tribune and notary, said: “Then let your subscriptions also be communicated to the judges, since declarations are likewise required from those who are present on their side.”

106. Petilianus, bishop, said: “They wish to give authorization in the records.” And in another hand: “I, Petilianus, have acknowledged it.”

107. Marcellinus, most illustrious man, tribune and notary, said: “In which records does Your Holiness assert that it will give authorization?”

108. Emeritus, bishop, said: “Our will lies in the judgment of your Excellence, if you order that this proceeding before your Nobility be concluded through the municipal records.” And in another hand: “I, Emeritus the bishop, have acknowledged it.”

109. Marcellinus, most illustrious man, tribune and notary, said: “What is now necessarily demanded of Your Holiness, in order to cut off every ambiguity, is that you state quite plainly whether the letter of authorization, read aloud with its subscriptions, is sufficient for you, or whether you also require the persons themselves to give authorization in the records.”

110. Petilianus, bishop, said: “We do not wish them to make a declaration, but to be recognized by us—the persons who are said to have given authorization.” And in another hand: “As above.”

111. Marcellinus, most illustrious man, tribune and notary, [Col. 1281A] said: “Then let the names of the subscribers be read in order.”

112. Honoratus, recorder, read: “Numidius, bishop of the Catholic Church of Maxula.” He said: “I am present.” Felix, bishop of the place named above, said: “I recognize him.” Marcellinus, most illustrious man, tribune and notary, said: “It is established that both are present.”

113. Alypius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “Let counterparts of those two who have already gone out also come forward. They themselves demanded this. Let it therefore be seen who are present and who are absent. This is what we wish to be established.” And in another hand: “I have acknowledged it.” And when a bishop approached:

114. Marcellinus, most illustrious man, tribune and notary, said: “Of what city is this venerable bishop?” Adeodatus, bishop, said: “Felix, bishop of Zumma, [Col. 1281B] [Note: [Col. 1281C] Of Zumma. In Numidia. Its bishop Silvanus was primate of Numidia.] of our communion, who is conducting proceedings against Silvanus, is unwell.”

115. Marcellinus, most illustrious man, tribune and notary, said: “That is a credible excuse.” And he added: “Let another be read.” And he read: “Marinus, bishop of the Church of Tabora.” He said: “I am present.” Victor, bishop of the city named above, said: “I recognize him.”

116. Marcellinus, most illustrious man, tribune and notary, said: “The records shall preserve the presence of both parties.” He then read: “Aurelius, bishop of the Catholic Church of the city of Magomaz.” [Note: [Col. 1281C] Magomaz, or Macomadia: a bishopric of Numidia, as is evident from chapter 182, where Aurelius says that he has a presbyter in the city of Idassa, a town of Numidia. The same follows from Antoninus and the list of African bishops, where Macomadia is found as a Numidian town distinct from the city of the same name in Byzacena.] He said: “I am present.” Marcellinus, most illustrious man, tribune and notary, said: “Let the other bishop of the same city come forward from the opposing party.” 261 Salustius, bishop of the party of Donatus in the city named above, said: “I recognize him.” Marcellinus, most illustrious man, [Col. 1281C] tribune and notary, said: “It is likewise established that these men are present.” He then read: “Victor, bishop of the Catholic Church of Libertina.” [Note: [Col. 1281C] Of Libertina. In the proconsular province. Januarius, bishop of Libertina, subscribed to the letter of the bishops of that province to Paul, patriarch of [Col. 1281D] Constantinople, which is reported in the Lateran Council under Martin.] He said: “I am present.” Januarius, bishop of the place named above, said: “I recognize him. It is my diocese.” Victor, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “He has no one there.” [Col. 1282A] Januarius, bishop of the party of Donatus, said: “It is my diocese.” Victor, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “Since he has no one there—neither a church nor anyone in communion with him—he lies in vain when he says that it is his diocese.” Januarius, bishop, said: “Did they communicate with you—or with me—before your violence?” [The transmitted text has *tibi (f mihi)*.]

117. Petilianus, bishop, said: “In the single congregation of our colleague Januarius, who is present, four have been set up against him in the one diocese, evidently in order that the number might be increased.”

118. Alypius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “Let inquiry be made how many years he has been a bishop.”

119. Petilianus, bishop, said: “You are four against one.”

120. Marcellinus, most illustrious man, tribune and notary, [Col. 1282B] said: “These matters have absolutely no bearing on the present proceeding. Let what has been begun be read through.” He then read: “Optatus, bishop of the people of Vescera.” [Note: [Col. 1281D] Of Vescera. This town appears to be the Numidian place called Bercerita in the list of African bishops. Baluzius conjectures that this Optatus is the man to whom Augustine’s Letter 190 was written.] He said: “I am present.” Fortunatus, bishop of the city named above, said: “I recognize him.” He then read: “Januarius, bishop of the people of Tunusuda.” [Note: [Col. 1281D] Of Tunusuda. An old manuscript reads Tunuda; but in chapter 201 Victorianus, bishop of this city on the Donatist side, is called bishop of Tunusuda. In Pliny, book V, chapter 4, Thunudis is listed among Roman towns in Africa; in Ptolemy, Thunusda. Victor of Vita, book I, §13, mentions Tinusada, or, as some manuscripts have it, Tunusuda. The city Thunu also occurs on the Peutinger Table. Some fail to distinguish it from Timida, a town in the proconsular province, but wrongly.] He said: “I am present.” Victorianus, bishop of the city named above, said: “I recognize him.” He then read: “Evangelus, [Note: [Col. 1282C] Evangelus. He attended the councils held at Carthage in 397 and 401. He occurs in canons 23 and 77 of the codex of canons of the African Church.] bishop of the Church of Assuras.” [Note: [Col. 1282C] Of the Church of Assuras. In the proconsular province. At the Council of Carthage under Cyprian, Victor of Assuras was present. There is also a letter of Cyprian himself to his brother Epictetus and to the people dwelling at Assuras.] He said: “I am present.” Petilianus, bishop, said: “Our man there has died.” [Note: [Col. 1282C] “Our man there has died.” This was Praetextatus, who subscribed to the Council of Cabarsussi in 393 and was removed from his see at Bagai in the following year. That he had died shortly before Augustine wrote his books Against the Letter of Parmenianus is evident from the end of book III. [Col. 1282D] He was succeeded by Rogatus, mentioned by Augustine in book III Against Cresconius, chapter 56. After Rogatus later converted to Catholic unity, the Circumcellions cut off his hands and tongue, as Augustine himself relates in *On the Proceedings with Emeritus*, §9.] He then read: “Latonius, bishop of the Church of the people of Thena.” [Note: [Col. 1282D] Of Thena. In the province of Byzacena, as the list of African bishops shows. At the Council of Carthage under Cyprian, Euchratius of Thena subscribed among the others. Pliny, Antoninus, and the Anonymous Cosmographer of Ravenna call it Thenae or Thaenae; Ptolemy, Theaenae.] He said: “I am present.” Securus, bishop of the city named above, said: “I recognize him.” He then read: “Aptus, bishop of the people of Tigi.” [Note: [Col. 1282D] Of Tigi, or Tisi, in Byzacena, as the list of African bishops shows.] He said: “I am present. I have not had, nor do we have, a Donatist bishop.” Primianus, bishop of Carthage, said: “We do not have one there.” He then read: “Assellicus, bishop of the Church of Tusura.” [Note: [Col. 1282D] Of Tusura. From the province of Arzugis, as is inferred from chapter 208. It was part of the province of Tripolitania, or at least adjacent to it, as is clear from chapter 49 of the Codex of Canons of the African Church.] He said: “I am present.” Aptus, bishop of the city named above, said: “I recognize him.” He then read: “Innocentius, bishop of the Church of Germana,” [Col. 1283A] [Note: [Col. 1283C] Of Germana. In Numidia, as the African list shows, distinct from Germaniciana in Byzacena.] He said: “I am present, but I have no opponent.” He then read: “Honoratus, bishop of the Church of Mathara.” [Note: [Col. 1283C] Of Mathara. In Numidia, as is written in the same list.] He said: “I am present, but I have no bishop opposed to me.” He then read: “Hilarus, bishop of the Church of Bofeta.” [Note: [Col. 1283C] Of Bofeta. Better, Boseta, in Numidia; it is mentioned in the acts of Saint Mammarius and his companions among the cities of Numidia near Tigisis.] He said: “I am present, but I do not have a bishop opposed to me.”

121. Petilianus, bishop, said: “He was ours.” Alypius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “And we desire that you should imitate him.” He then read: “Secundus, bishop of the Church of Ruspe.” [Note: [Col. 1283C] Of Ruspe. The list of Byzacena has a bishop of Rusfa or Ruspe; but Ptolemy distinguishes Ruspina from Ruspe, and both occur in the Peutinger Table and in the Anonymous Cosmographer of Ravenna; both are in Byzacena.] He said: “I am present, but I have no bishop opposed to me.” He then read: “Donatus, bishop of the Church of Ambura.” [Note: [Col. 1283C] Of Ambura. The list of Numidia has Ampora, and that is how it should be read; for below Servatus, who is said here to be bishop of the same see, is called Amphorensis in an old copy.] He said: “I am present.” Servatus, bishop of the city named above, said: “I recognize him.” He then read: “Cresconius, bishop of the Church of Tubuna.” [Note: [Col. 1283C] Of Tubuna, or Tubuni, in Numidia, as the list shows; distinct from Tubia in Mauretania. Among the bishops at the Council of Carthage under Cyprian is Nemesianus of Tubuna. [Col. 1283D] At Tubuna Augustine held a discussion with Count Boniface, who then wished, having abandoned all worldly affairs, to embrace monastic life. On this, see Augustine, Letter 229.] [Col. 1283B] He said: “I am present.” Protasius, bishop of the city named above, said: “I recognize him.” He then read: “Restitutus, bishop of the people of Novasa.” [Note: [Col. 1283D] Of Novasa, or Nobasa, in Numidia, as the list shows.] He said: “I am present.” Felix, bishop of the city named above, said: “I recognize him.” He then read: “Cresconius, bishop of the Church of Cuicul.” [Note: [Col. 1283D] Of Cuicul. In the same place, according to the same list. At the Council of Carthage under Cyprian, Pudentianus of Cuicul was present.] He said: “I am present. I had a bishop opposed to me; he has departed from the body.” He then read: “Lucianus, bishop of the Church of Guira.” [Note: [Col. 1283D] Of Guira. Guira is an African city on the Peutinger Table. Perhaps Girensis should be read, whose bishop Martialis occurs in the Numidian list.] He said: “I am present, but I have no other bishop opposed to me.” He then read: “Tutus, bishop of the people of Melzita.” [Note: [Col. 1283D] Of Melzita. Pliny and Ptolemy mention the African town Meldita, located among the inland cities of the proconsular province.] He said: “I am present, but I have no other bishop opposed to me.” He then read: “Donatianus, bishop of the Church of Telepte.” [Note: [Col. 1283D] Of Telepte. Telepte was a very well-known city in Byzacena. Nor was Donatianus, its bishop, obscure: he was primate of the province and attended several African councils.] He said: “I am present.” Bellicius, bishop of the city [Col. 1284A] named above, 262 said: “I recognize him.” He then read: “Potentius, bishop of the people of Blada.” [Note: [Col. 1283D] Of Blada. Baluzius considers that Bada should be read, and that the opponent of this Potentius was Pancratius of Bada, named below in chapter 180. Dativus of Bada attended the Council of Carthage under Cyprian. The Anonymous Cosmographer of Ravenna places Bada in Mauretania Gaditana; for this reason the see of Bada may be distinct from Vada in Numidia, mentioned in the list.] He said: “I am present.” Adeodatus, bishop, said: “The man we have there has sore eyes and cannot come.” Alypius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “Is he here in Carthage?” He then read: “Maximianus, bishop of the people of Tura.” [Note: [Col. 1284C] Of Tura, or Turra, in Byzacena, as may be seen in the African list.] He said: “I am present, but I have no bishop opposed to me.” Adeodatus, bishop, said: “He was ours.” He then read: “Datianus, bishop of the people of Lega.” [Note: [Col. 1284C] Of Lega. The Numidian list contains two cities of this name: no. 78, Legia, and no. 85, Lega. Likewise, there are here two bishops of these cities: in this chapter Dacianus, bishop of Lega, who has no opponent; and in chapter 187 Cresconius, Donatist bishop of Lega.] He said: “I am present, but I have no other bishop opposed to me.” He then read: “Urbicus, bishop of the people of Theveste.” [Note: [Col. 1284C] Of Theveste. Theveste is a well-known city in Numidia; see what we said in note 44 to book III of Optatus, p. 41.] He said: “I am present.” Perseverantius, bishop of the city named above, said: “I recognize him.” He then read: “Aspidius, bishop of the people of Tacarata.” [Note: [Col. 1284C] Of Tacarata. In Numidia, as the list shows. He was one of the four bishops whom Verissimus complained had been established by the Catholics in this diocese. [Col. 1284D] Octavianus is later called bishop of Ressia, and Fortunatus bishop of Casa.] He said: “I am present.” Verissimus, [Col. 1284B] bishop of the city named above, said: “I recognize him. There are four in my congregation: Datianus, Aspidius, Fortunatus, and Octavianus.” He then read: “Terentius, bishop of Seleucia.” [Note: [Col. 1284D] Of Seleucia. Likewise in Numidia. In the same list.] He said: “I am present.” Mescianus, bishop of the city named above, said: “I recognize him.” He then read: “Servus Dei, bishop of the people of Tubursicum Bure.” [Note: [Col. 1284D] Of Tubursicum Bure. Augustine, book III *Against Cresconius*, calls the Catholic bishop of Tubursicum Bure Servus. That this Church belonged to the proconsular province is proved from the Council of Carthage under Boniface, at which Reparatus, bishop of Tubursicum Bure, was present among the other bishops of that province.] He said: “I am present.” Donatus, bishop of the city named above, said: “I recognize him.” He then read: “Dialogus, bishop of Zama.” [Note: [Col. 1284D] Of Zama. Zama was a royal city in Numidia, as is evident from Ptolemy and the Peutinger Table.] He said: “I am present.” Montanus, bishop of the city named above, said: “I recognize him.” He then read: “Urbicosus, bishop of the people of Eguilguil.” [Note: [Col. 1284D] Of Eguilguil. Igilgita should be read: for Igilgilis, a town in Mauretania Sitifensis, is mentioned by Ptolemy, in Antoninus’s *Itinerary*, on the Peutinger Table, and by the Anonymous Cosmographer of Ravenna. Ammianus Marcellinus, book XX, chapter 5, mentions the coast of Mauretania Sitifensis, which the inhabitants call Igilgitan. There is also an Igilgitan bishop in the list of Mauretania Sitifensis.] He said: “I am present, but the whole place has from ancient times been Catholic.” He then read: “Silvanus, bishop [Col. 1285A] of the people of Perdix.” [Note: [Col. 1285C] Of Perdix. Antoninus, in the *Itinerary*, mentions Perdix between Zara and Sitifis, twenty-five Roman miles from the latter. At the Council of Carthage of 403, Silvanus, legate of the province of Mauretania Sitifensis, was present; he does not seem to be different from this man.] He said: “I am present.” Rogatus, bishop of the city named above, said: “I recognize him.” He then read: “Navigius, bishop of Dydris.” [Note: [Col. 1285C] Of Dydris. Baluzius rightly conjectures that Thusdris should be read; for nowhere is a city called Dydris mentioned in Africa, and later, in chapter 206, Honoratus, who is here called the opponent of Navigius, bishop of Dydris, is called bishop of Thusdris. Ptolemy mentions the town of Thusdris, and Antoninus’s *Itinerary* places it among the towns of the province of Byzacena.] He said: “I am present.” Honoratus, bishop of the city named above, said: “I recognize him.” He then read: “Romanus, bishop of the people of Leptiminus.” [Note: [Col. 1285C] Of Leptiminus. A town in the province of Byzacena, so likewise named in the list. In Ptolemy and Antoninus, Leptis Minor; in the Anonymous Cosmographer of Ravenna, following the Peutinger Table, Lepte Minus. At the Council of Carthage under Cyprian, Demetrius of Leptiminus gave his judgment. The ancients also mention two Leptises in Africa, the Lesser and the Great. The latter is called Leptimagna in the list and belongs to the province of Tripolitania.] He said: “I am present.” Victorinus, bishop of the city named above, said: “I recognize him.” He then read: “Rufinus, bishop of the people of Drusiliana.” [Note: [Col. 1285D] Of Drusiliana. Drusiliana is named after Tatiam, a city in the proconsular province, on the Peutinger Table and in the Anonymous Cosmographer of Ravenna.] He said: “I am present.” Restitutus, bishop of the city named above, said: “I recognize him.” He then read: “Donatus, bishop of Tisili.” [Note: [Col. 1285D] Of Tisili. This man is different from the bishop of Tibili. For this Donatus says here that he has no opponent; yet in chapter 197 Simpliplicius, Donatist bishop of Tibili, is named. Florentius, bishop of Tisili, is recorded as present at the Council of Carthage under Boniface in 525. I would judge this bishopric to have belonged to the proconsular province.] He said: “I am present, but I have no other bishop opposed to me.” Petilianus, the Donatist bishop, said: “He has departed from the body.” He then read: “Gallus, bishop of Tice,” [Col. 1285B] [Note: [Col. 1285D] Of Tice. The Anonymous Cosmographer of Ravenna mentions Tices in Gaetulia; Ptolemy calls it the city of Ticena. The list of African Byzacena mentions a city called Ticibus. In the synodal letter of the Byzacene fathers in act 2 of the Lateran Council under Martin, the subscriptions are read: Romulus, [Col. 1286C] bishop of the city of Ticibus, and Candidus, bishop of his native city of Dice. If *Ticensis* should be read for *Dicensis*, as Baluzius conjectures, Tice would be distinct from Ticibus; yet this does not seem likely to me.] He said: “I am present.” Petilianus, bishop, said: “He did not come; he sent a letter.” He then read: “Donatianus, bishop of Monta.” [Note: [Col. 1286C] Of Monta, or Montensis: a bishop in Numidia, as the list shows.] He said: “I am present.” Petilianus, bishop, said: “He is ill.” He then read: “Victorianus, bishop of the people of Mustis.” [Note: [Col. 1286C] Of Mustis. A bishop of Mustis occurs in the Numidian list; but there was another Mustis situated in the proconsular province, as may be inferred from Antoninus’s *Itinerary*. Its bishop here is Januarius, who had two Donatist opponents, Felicianus of Mustis and Donatus of Tura. In the other Mustis, in Numidia, the bishop was Donatianus; not Felicianus, but Cresconius, as is read in chapter 206. Augustine frequently mentions the Mustitans and Assuritans together in his books against the Donatists. The Assuritans belonged to the proconsular province.] He said: “I am present. I have Felicianus of Mustis and Donatus of Tura [Note: [Col. 1286C] Of Tura. This place seems distinct from the city of Tura in the province of Byzacena, since it was adjacent to [Col. 1286D] the city of Mustis, which was in the proconsular province. The bishop of this see appears to have been Samfucius, whom Augustine discusses in Letters 34 and 83.] opposed to me.”

122. Alypius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “Concerning Felicianus: whether he is in the communion of Primianus.” And in another hand: “I have acknowledged it.”

123. Petilianus, bishop, said: “Who instructed you to ask this, or on whose behalf do you demand it? Or do you wish to assume the role of those who are outside?” And in another hand: “I, Petilianus the bishop, have acknowledged it.”

124. Alypius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “Let an answer be given to what has been requested.” [Col. 1286A] And in another hand: “I have acknowledged it.”

125. Petilianus, bishop, said: “This already belongs to the internal proceeding.” And in another hand: “As above.”

126. Marcellinus, most illustrious man, tribune and notary, said: Let the order already begun now be maintained. If it seems reasonable, inquiry into these matters may be made afterward. Likewise he read:

Victorianus, bishop of the people of Mustis, in place of 263 Paschasius, bishop of the people of Anguia.  
[Note: **[Col. 1286D] Of the Anguienses.** To which province it belongs is uncertain.]

The same Paschasius said: I am present; I hold to unity.

Likewise he read:

Ferox, bishop of the people of Greater Macriana.  
[Note: **[Col. 1286D] Of Greater Macriana.** In Byzacena, as is clear from the *Notitia*.]

The same said: I am present; I hold to unity.

Pomponius, bishop, said: I recognize him.  
[Note: **[Col. 1286D] Pomponius of Macriana,** who attended the Council of Cabarsussa.]

Likewise he read:

Asmunius, bishop of Tigualis.  
[Note: **[Col. 1286D] Of Tigualis, or Ticualta.** In the province of Byzacena, as the *Notitia*, no. 95, shows.]

The same said: I am present. In my diocese [Col. 1286B] there are two, Gaianus and Privatus.

Gaianus, bishop of the aforesaid place, said: I recognize him.

Alypius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: Your nobility observes that they have also ordained bishops in the dioceses belonging to us.

And in another hand: I have checked it.

Marcellinus, most illustrious man, tribune and notary, said: It is evident that such charges are made by both sides, so that, if you wish these matters to be investigated carefully, we shall be seen to have come to this case unnecessarily.

Likewise he read:

Felix, bishop of the people of Segermis.  
[Note: **[Col. 1286D] Of Segermis, or Segermitanus.** In the province of Byzacena according to the *Notitia*. At the Council of Carthage under Cyprian, Nicomedes of Segermis delivered an opinion.]

The same said: I am present.

Restitutus, bishop of the aforesaid place, said: I recognize him.

Likewise he read:

Secundus, bishop of the people of Magarmela.  
[Note: **[Col. 1286D] Of Magarmela.** In the *Notitia* of Numidia it is called Vagarmelitanus. Secundus may perhaps be the man who subscribed Leporius’s petition in these words: “Secundus, bishop of the Church of Aquae, or Megarmita.”]

The same said: I am present.

Felix, bishop of the aforesaid place, said: I recognize him.

Likewise he read:

Vincentianus, bishop of the people of Greater Feradita [Col. 1287A].  
[Note: **[Col. 1287B] Of Greater Feradita.** In the *Notitia* of the bishops of Byzacena it is called Feradimaiensis.]

The same said: I am present; I hold to unity.

Likewise he read:

Placentinus, bishop of the people of Madaura.  
[Note: **[Col. 1287B] Of Madaura.** Madaura, a city of Numidia, illustrious as the birthplace of Apuleius and for Augustine’s studies there. Saint Augustine defends the martyrs of Madaura in Epistle 17. Antigonus, bishop of Madaura, attended the Council of Carthage under Gratus; and among the exiled bishops of the province of Numidia, the name of Pudentius of Madaura appears in the *Notitia*.]

The same said: I am present.

Donatus, bishop of the aforesaid place, said: I recognize him.

Likewise he read:

Rusticianus, bishop of the people of Tabraca.  
[Note: **[Col. 1287B] Of Tabraca.** Tabraca was a city known to ancient authors, between Proconsular Africa and Numidia; its bishop Victoricus of Tabraca [Col. 1287C] delivered an opinion at the Council of Carthage under Cyprian. It belonged to the proconsular province.]

The same said: I am present.

Clarentius, bishop of the aforesaid place, said: I recognize him.

Likewise he read:

Octavianus, bishop of the people of Ressia.  
[Note: **[Col. 1287C] Of Ressia.** In Numidia. This Octavianus is one of the four bishops whom Verissimus of Tacarata had earlier complained had been installed by Catholics in his diocese.]

The same said: I am present; I hold to unity.

Likewise he read:

Benenatus, bishop of the people of Simmitthus.  
[Note: **[Col. 1287C] Of Simmitthus.** In the proconsular province, as is evident from Ptolemy and the Antonine Itinerary. In the *Notitia* of the proconsular province there are two sees whose names are close to this: no. 37, Simminensis, and no. 42, Seminensis. Benenatus, the bishop mentioned here, appears to have been one of the four who undertook an embassy at the Council of Carthage in 410.]

The same said: I am present, and I have neither another bishop nor heretics.

Petilianus, bishop, said: He has departed from the body.

Likewise he read:

Timianus, bishop of the people of Utma.  
[Note: **[Col. 1287C] Of Utma.** The name of the town Utimmira in the proconsular province appears in the *Notitia*; it may perhaps not be different from Utma.]

The same said: I am present.

Petilianus, bishop, said: He has Felix, but he is absent.

Likewise he read:

Filolocius, bishop of the people of Hadrumetum [Col. 1287B].  
[Note: **[Col. 1287C–D] Philolocius, bishop of the people of Hadrumetum.** At the Council of Carthage in 403 he is called Philologius, one of the bishops of the province of Byzacena.]

The same said: I am present.

Victorinus, bishop of the aforesaid city, said: I recognize him.

Likewise he read:

Adeodatus, bishop of the people of Belalis.  
[Note: **[Col. 1287D] Of Belalis.** In the *Notitia* of the bishops of Numidia there is a see called Belesasensis, which Baluzius suspects is the same as this one.]

The same said: I am present; I have neither a bishop nor heretics; I hold to unity.

Likewise he read:

Felix, bishop of the people of Visica.  
[Note: **[Col. 1287D] Of Visica.** In the letter of the bishops of the proconsular province to Patriarch Paul, Valentinianus, bishop of the Church of Visica, subscribes.]

The same said: I am present; [Col. 1288A] I have no bishop against me.

Victor, bishop of the city of Tabora, said: A short while ago he departed; I serve there in his place.  
[Note: **[Col. 1287D–1288B] Victor, bishop of the city of Tabora.** He is a Donatist bishop of a neighboring city, since he immediately says that, after the departure of the bishop of Visica, he himself takes charge of that people. For this is what the following words mean: “He departed recently,” that is, he died; “I serve there,” that is, I care for the people, as below, chapter 176: “We have a presbyter who serves in his place.” Since, therefore, the town of Visica belongs to the proconsular province, the see of Tabora must belong to the same province and is consequently different from Taborentum, which is found in the *Notitia* of Mauretania Caesariensis.]

Likewise he read:

Victor, bishop of the people of Jufita.  
[Note: **[Col. 1288B] Of Jufita.** In the *Notitia* of Mauretania Sitifensis there is a Victor of Jerafita; perhaps Jerafitensis should be read here.]

The same said: I am present; we hold to unity.

Likewise he read:

Fuscinullus, bishop of the people of Elia.  
[Note: **[Col. 1288B] Of Elia.** In Byzacena, as the *Notitia* shows. In the Antonine Itinerary and in the anonymous Ravennate there is a city Elie. Constantine, bishop of the holy Church of Helia, subscribes to the synodical letter of the bishops of Byzacena to Constantine, read at the Lateran Council under Martin.]

The same said: I am present; I have no bishop against me.

Likewise he read:

Honorius, bishop of the people of Cella.  
[Note: **[Col. 1288B–C] Of Cella.** There were two African Churches of this name: one in the proconsular province, the other in Sitifensis. It is uncertain which is meant here.]

The same said: I am present.

Castus, bishop, said: I recognize him.

Likewise he read:

Maximianus, bishop of Aquae Regiae.  
[Note: **[Col. 1288C] Of Aquae Regiae.** Aquae Regiae was a town in the province of Byzacena, according to the Peutinger Table, Antoninus, and the *Notitia*. This Maximianus attended the seventh Council of Carthage in 419 under Aurelius as legate in the name of the province of Byzacena; see the *Code of Canons of the African Church*, canon 127, where he is called bishop of Aquae, and in certain manuscripts bishop of Aquae Regiae or of Aquae-Regiae.]

The same said: I am present; in my own country I have no other bishop.

Likewise he read:

Antonius, bishop of the people of Carpita.  
[Note: **[Col. 1288C] Of Carpita.** A see in the proconsular province; see what we said on Book II of Optatus, p. 42, note 46.]

The same said: I am present.

Veratianus, bishop, said: I recognize him.

Likewise he read:

Fortunatianus, bishop of the people of Neapolis [Col. 1288B].  
[Note: **[Col. 1288C–D] Of Neapolis.** Likewise in the proconsular province, as the *Notitia* shows. Fortunatianus, bishop of Neapolis, attended the Council of Carthage under Cyprian. Hirtius in his book on the African War, Pomponius Mela, and other authors mention this city; the Antonine Itinerary and the Peutinger Tables place it midway between Putput and Clypea. Ptolemy, however, calls Neapolis a colony, and Pliny a free town.]

The same said: I am present.

Ampelius, bishop of the aforesaid city, said: I recognize him.

Likewise he read:

Pannonius, bishop of the people of Puppita.  
[Note: **[Col. 1288D] Of Puppita.** A city of the proconsular province, called Putput in the Antonine Itinerary, Pudput in the Peutinger Tables, Pulpu in the anonymous Ravennate, and Pulpud by Cyprian and Titus Livy. The name of this Pannonius may be read in the letter of the Council of Carthage to Pope Innocent, among Epistle 175 in the latest edition, where the name Pannonius was restored from manuscripts, having previously been incorrectly read as Pantonius. At the Council of Carthage in 525 under Boniface, Fortunatus, bishop of the people of Puppita, attended; and Gulosus, bishop of Puppita, is the first of all to subscribe to the synodical letter of the bishops of the proconsular province read at the Lateran Council.]

The same said: I am present.

Victorianus, bishop of the aforesaid city, 264 said: I recognize him.

Likewise he read:

Januarianus, bishop of the people of Tubulbaca.  
[Note: **[Col. 1288D] Of Tubulbaca.** In Byzacena, as the *Notitia* shows.]

The same said: I am present; unity is Catholic; [Col. 1289A] I have no bishop against me in my city.

Likewise he read:

Gratianus, bishop of the people of Meta.  
[Note: **[Col. 1289B] Of Meta.** In the province of Numidia, as may be seen in the same *Notitia*.]

The same said: I am present.

Fortunatianus, bishop of the party of Donatus in the aforesaid city, said: I recognize him.

Likewise he read:

Victor, bishop of the people of Bahanna.  
[Note: **[Col. 1289B] Of Bahanna.** In the *Notitia* of the province of Byzacena there is a see of Boana, and Januarius, bishop of Bana, subscribes to the letter of the bishops of this province to Constantine at the Lateran Council under Martin.]

The same said: I am present; I hold to unity.

Likewise he read:

Quodvultdeus, bishop of the people of Centuria.  
[Note: **[Col. 1289C] Of Centuria.** In Numidia, as the *Notitia* shows; and Procopius, Book II of the *Vandalic War*, mentions a certain fortress called Centuriae in Numidia. This same Quodvultdeus, bishop of Centuria, was dealt with at the Council of Milevis in 402, *Code of the African Church*, canon 87, which decrees that no one should communicate with him until his case had been resolved, because he had refused to contend with his opponent before the judgment of bishops.]

The same said: I am present.

Cresconius, bishop of the party of Donatus in the aforesaid city, said: I recognize him.

Likewise he read:

Fortunatus, bishop of the people of Capsa.  
[Note: **[Col. 1289C–D] Of Capsa.** Capsa was a city in the province of Byzacena. Most ancient writers mention it. Donatulus of Capsa subscribes to the Council of Carthage under Cyprian, who also mentions the city of Capsa in Epistle 56. In the *Notitia* of the province of Byzacena, no. 60, the see of Capsa occurs. Ptolemy lists Capsa among the cities situated under Hadrumetum. The treasures of King Jugurtha were kept there, as Strabo testifies, Book XVII. Sallust says of this city in his *Jugurthine War*: “Amid immense deserts there was a great and powerful town named Capsa.” He afterward describes its destruction, as does Florus, Book III, chapter 1. Pliny, Book V, chapter 4, mentions the Capsitani [Col. 1289D] among those who may properly be called not merely cities but for the most part even nations. The Peutinger Tables call Capsa a colony.]

The same said: I am present.

Celer, bishop of the party of Donatus in the aforesaid city, said: I recognize him.

Likewise he read:

Cresconius, bishop of the people of Temonia.  
[Note: **[Col. 1289D] Of Temonia.** A see of the province of Byzacena, as the *Notitia* shows, although there it is read Themoniarensis. In the synodical letter of the bishops of Byzacena to Constantine, Victorinus of Themunia is found among the bishops. Cresconius, mentioned here, was chosen as legate of the province of Byzacena, *Code of the African Church*, canon 127.]

The same said: I am present. There, in the same place where I reside, I have no bishop against me [Col. 1289B].

Likewise he read:

Montanus, bishop of the Catholic Church of Augura.  
[Note: **[Col. 1289D] Of Augura.** In Numidia, as is evident from the *Notitia*. Earlier it was wrongly read Cathauguritensis.]

The same said: I am present; I hold to unity.

Likewise he read:

Jocundus, bishop of the people of Sufetula.  
[Note: **[Col. 1289D] Jocundus, bishop of the people of Sufetula.** In the province of Byzacena; he attended the Council of Carthage in 419. Privatianus of Sufetula sat at the Council of Carthage under Cyprian. Praesidius of Sufetula is named in the *Notitia* of the bishops of the province of Byzacena, and Victor of Vita celebrates the place in Book II of his *Vandalic History*.]

The same said: I am present.

Titianus, bishop of the party of Donatus in the aforesaid city [Col. 1290A], said: I recognize him.

Likewise he read:

Victor, bishop of the people of Bartana.  
[Note: **[Col. 1290B] Of Bartana.** To which province it belongs is uncertain.]

The same said: I am present.

Honorius, bishop of the party of Donatus in the aforesaid city, said: Only now have I learned of the wrongs which he has done me.

Likewise he read:

Victor, bishop of Cullita.  
[Note: **[Col. 1290B] Of Cullita.** Perhaps Cululitanus, who is listed among the bishops of the province of Byzacena in the *Notitia*, no. 56. Procopius, Book VI of Justinian’s *Buildings*, lists Cululis among the inland cities of Byzacena which that emperor had fortified against the Moors.]

The same said: I am present.

Fidentius, bishop of the aforesaid city, said: I recognize him.

Likewise he read:

Palatinus, bishop of Boseta.  
[Note: **[Col. 1290B–C] Of Boseta.** There was a bishopric of this name in the proconsular province as well as in Numidia. For in the letter of the bishops of the proconsular province at the Lateran Council under Martin is read the subscription of Cresciturus, bishop of the Church of Busita, or, as the Beauvais manuscript has it, Bosita. His opponent Felix is called below, chapter 202, Vosetanus.]

The same said: I am present.

Felix, bishop of the aforesaid city, said: I recognize him.

Likewise he read:

Quodvultdeus, bishop of Girba.  
[Note: **[Col. 1290C] Of Girba.** Thus Baluzius corrected it, for the manuscript reads Givit. At the Council of Carthage under Cyprian, Monnulus of Girba delivered an opinion. At the Council of Cabarsussa, Proculus was bishop of Girba. Evasius, here said to be Quodvultdeus’s opponent in chapter 199, is called bishop of Girba. At the Council of Carthage under Boniface in 525, Vincentius, bishop of the people of Gervita or Girba in the province of Tripolitania, attended as legate. In the *Notitia* of this province there is a bishop of Girba; likewise, in section 42 of the *Notitia of the Empire*, a procurator of the Girbitan dye-works in the province of Tripolitania is mentioned.]

The same said: I am present.

Evasius, bishop of the aforesaid city, said: I recognize him.

Likewise he read:

Silvamus, bishop of Cariana.  
[Note: **[Col. 1290C–D] Of Cariana,** or of the Carian Casulae. A town in the province of Byzacena.]

The same said: I am present; unity is there.

Likewise he read:

Aemilianus, bishop of Aggerita [Col. 1290B].  
[Note: **[Col. 1290D] Of Aggerita.** In the *Notitia* of the province of Byzacena there are two sees of Aggarita, nos. 29 and 108; Aemilianus was bishop of one or the other.]

The same said: I am present.

Candorius, bishop of the aforesaid city, said: I recognize him.

Likewise he read:

Privatus, bishop of the people of Usila.  
[Note: **[Col. 1290D] Of Usila.** In the *Notitia* of the province of Byzacena, Usulensis. Cassianus of Usila was present at the Council of Carthage under Gratus, and Theodore of Usila, a known Donatist, subscribed to the Council of Cabarsussa. Yet the manuscript of the Colbert Library reads Uculensis, a city in the proconsular province distinct from Usila; its bishop was Cericius, of whom see below, chapter 128. In the synodical letter of the bishops of Byzacena, Laurentius, bishop of the city of Usilabis, subscribes; and in the letter of the bishops of the proconsular province, Cresconius, bishop of the Church of Ucula. Ptolemy mentions Οὐσίλλα (*Usilla*). Antoninus places the city Usula between Thysdrus and Thennae. The anonymous Ravennate calls it Usila, and the Peutinger Tables Usilla.]

The same said: I am present; I have no bishop against me.

Petilianus, bishop [Col. 1291A], said: He has a presbyter there.

Likewise he read:

Maius, bishop of the people of Amudarsa.  
[Note: **[Col. 1291B] Of Amudarsa.** Amudarsa, or Amurdasa, was a city of the province of Byzacena in Ptolemy and the Antonine Itinerary. In the *Notitia* of the same province Liberatus of Amudarsa appears.]

The same said: I am present; in my country it is Catholic.

Likewise he read:

Victor, bishop of the people of Uvaza.  
[Note: **[Col. 1291B] Of Uvaza.** In the proconsular province. For Ptolemy, Book IV, chapter 3, mentions the city of Vazna between the city of Thabraca and the river Bagradas; it therefore seems to have lain on the border of the proconsular province toward Numidia. Thus Baluzius.]

The same said: I am present.

Secundinus, bishop of the aforesaid people, said: I recognize him.

Likewise he read:

Cresconius, bishop of the people of Titulus.  
[Note: **[Col. 1291C] Of Titulus.** In the proconsular province there is a bishop of Titulus.]

The same said: I am present.

Victor, bishop of the aforesaid place, said: I recognize him.

Likewise he read:

Milicus, bishop of the people of Tagamuta.  
[Note: **[Col. 1291C] Of Tagamuta.** In the province of Byzacena, as is clear from the *Notitia*, no. 19.]

The same said: I am present; all are Catholics.

Likewise he read:

Speratus, bishop of the people of Ammaedara.  
[Note: **[Col. 1291C] Of Ammaedara.** Ptolemy calls it Ammaedara and places it after Sicca Veneria, Assuras, Naraggara, and Madaura—that is, on the border between the proconsular province and Numidia. The Antonine Itinerary places Ammaedara among the cities of Numidia.]

The same said: I am present.

Crescentianus, bishop of the aforesaid city, said: I recognize him.

Likewise he read:

Aurelius, bishop of the people of Numnula.  
[Note: **[Col. 1291C] Of Numnula.** In the proconsular province, as is clear from the letter of the bishops of that province at the Lateran Council, in which Donatianus, bishop of the Church of Numnula, subscribes.]

The same said: I am present [Col. 1291B] 265; I have no bishop against me.

Habetdeus, deacon of Primianus, bishop of Carthage, said: He has departed from the body.

Likewise he read:

Venustus, bishop of the people of Turuda.  
[Note: **[Col. 1291C] Of Turuda.** Perhaps Turusensis in the proconsular province.]

The same said: I am present.

Adeodatus, bishop, said: We have none there.

Likewise he read:

Honoratus, bishop of Abidda.  
[Note: **[Col. 1291C–D] Of Abidda.** In the proconsular province, where there was a town Abitta, as Ptolemy and the Antonine Itinerary attest. Tertullus, bishop of Abitta, subscribes to the Council of Cabarsussa. There was also a bishop of Bidis or Biddis in Mauretania Caesariensis, and likewise one of Itis. Perhaps the reference might be assigned to either of these.]

The same said: I am present; I have no bishop against me there.

Likewise he read:

Gududus, bishop of Ancusa.  
[Note: **[Col. 1291D] Of Ancusa.** In the province of Byzacena. An old manuscript incorrectly reads Anusiensis here; for Donatus, Gududus’s opponent, is called bishop of Ancusa in chapter 207, as Baluzius correctly observed.]

The same said: I am present.

Donatus, bishop of the same place, said: I recognize him.

Likewise he read:

Sabratius, bishop of the people of Turris Tamallum.  
[Note: **[Col. 1291D–1292B] Of Turris Tamallum.** There were two African cities called Tamalluma, as is clear from the *Notitia*: one in the province of Byzacena, the other in Mauretania Sitifensis. The former is called Turris Tamallum. Vincentius of Girba, from the Council of Zunca, had seized the people of the Church of Tamallum. From this it is inferred that this city lay in the farthest parts of Byzacena toward Tripolitania, [Col. 1292B] to which Girba belonged. In the Antonine Itinerary, Turris Tamalleni is placed on the frontier of Tripolitania. At the Lateran Council under Martin, act 2, Pentasius, bishop of the holy Church of Turriumtamulus—or Turrium-Tamal, according to the Beauvais manuscript—subscribes to the letter of the Byzacenes.]

The same said [Col. 1292A]: I am present.

Jurata, bishop of the aforesaid city, said: I recognize him.

Likewise he read:

Fortunatus, bishop of the Church of Undesita.  
[Note: **[Col. 1292B–C] Of Undesita.** Vadesita should be read, as Baluzius notes. For later Cresconius, Fortunatus’s opponent, is called Baiesitanus in chapter 201; and indeed in the *Notitia* of African bishops no Undesitanus occurs, but a Vadesitanus occurs among the Numidians.]

The same said: I am present.

Cresconias, bishop [of the aforesaid place], said: I recognize him.

Likewise he read:

Severus, bishop of the people of Utimara.  
[Note: **[Col. 1292C] Of Utimara.** In the third *Notitia* of the proconsular province there is a bishop of Utimmira, but we have determined that Timianus of Utma, mentioned above, was bishop of this see.]

The same said: I am present; unity is there.

Likewise he read:

Paschasius, bishop of the people of Tijuca.  
[Note: **[Col. 1292C] Of Tijuca.** The name of this see does not appear in the *Notitia*. For Baluzius, in taking the Tisiensis to belong to Byzacena, failed to notice that above Apto, bishop of the people of Tigiensis, had assigned himself to that see. I would think that the town Tysica—which Augustine teaches was situated in the proconsular province, and over which, he says, Novellus was bishop in Caecilian’s time—was distinct from Tisium and was identical with the Tijuca now under discussion.]

The same said: I am present, but unity is there.

Likewise he read:

Valerius, bishop of the people of Utinisa.  
[Note: **[Col. 1292C] Of Utinisa.** Perhaps Tinnisensis in the proconsular province.]

The same said: I am present; I have no bishop.

Habeldeus, deacon, said: He was there; he has departed from the body.

Likewise he read:

Urbanus, bishop of the people of Theudala.  
[Note: **[Col. 1292C–D] Of Theudala.** That the city Theudala was in the proconsular province is clear from Ptolemy, Book IV, chapter 3, and Pliny, Book V, chapter 4. Victor of Vita, Book I, no. 7, praises Habetdeus, bishop of Theudala, who was banished by Genseric. Baluzius and Hardouin judge that Theudalensis should be read in place of Eudalensis in the *Notitia* of the proconsular province.]

The same said: I am present. Catholic unity is there.

Likewise he read:

Victor, bishop of the people of Migirpa.  
[Note: **[Col. 1292D] Of Migirpa.** In the proconsular province. Felix Primus of Migirpa subscribes to the Council of Carthage under Cyprian, and Migirpensis occurs in the *Notitia* of the bishops of the proconsular province. Tutus, bishop of Migirpa, attended the Council of Carthage in 397.]

The same said: I am present [Col. 1292B].

Gloriosus, bishop of the aforesaid place, said: I recognize him.

127. Fortunatianus, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: Since a conference of bishops has been requested, we are astonished that, by some sort of audacity, the deacon now present should wish to assume the role of a bishop [Note: **[Col. 1292D] The deacon now present.** Habetdeus, deacon of Primianus of Carthage, whose very many interventions survive in these proceedings.] and to disturb, through a zeal for contention, the conference which, with God’s favor, we have begun. Therefore let him restrain himself from such conduct, because it is unfitting to mingle unnecessary matters with serious business.

And in another hand: I have checked it.

128. Marcellinus, most illustrious man, tribune and notary, said: “Your Holiness pursues superfluous matters, since it is agreed that the man present was selected for this purpose: to identify each individual, not to take up the business of disputation.” Again he read:

Lucianus, bishop of the people of Tunes.

[Note: [Col. 1293B] **Tuneiensis.** Tunes is celebrated in Polybius; he describes its position thus: “Tunes is about 120 stadia from Carthage, and can be seen from almost every part of Carthage.” It is now Tunis. At the Fifth Ecumenical Council Sextilianus, bishop of Tunes, or Tunis, acted as representative for Primosus, bishop of Carthage.]

[He said:] “I am present; there is unity there.”

Again he read:

Donatus, bishop of the people of Saia.

[Note: [Col. 1293C] **Saiensis.** Holstenius thinks that *Saiensis* should be read as *Salditanus*, belonging to Mauretania Sitifensis; Baluzius proposes *Suensis*, the bishop of whose see we read as having subscribed in the letter of the bishops of the proconsular province to Paul the patriarch at the Lateran Council under Martin.]

He said: “I am present; there is unity there.”

Again he read:

Rufinianus, bishop of the people of Muzua.

[Note: [Col. 1293C] **Rufinianus, etc., Muzuensis.** He attended the Council of Carthage under Aurelius in the year 419, where the name of his see is variously reported. In Labbe’s edition, vol. II of the Councils, cols. 1603 and 1605, he is called Rufinianus of Muzuta, or Musta; and at col. 1670, Rufinus, bishop of Maza. In canon 127 of the Code of Canons of the African Church, he is called Muzucensis and is placed among the delegates of the proconsular province. Yet Muzuca belonged to Byzacena. Therefore, more correctly, in the Greek both here and in the subscriptions he is called Μουζουενσιανός, “of Muzua”; this accords with the Conference and the *Notitia*.]

He said: “I am present; the whole place is Catholic.”

Again he read:

Victor, bishop of the people of Trisipa.

[Note: [Col. 1293C–D] **Trisipensis.** This see is mentioned nowhere else except in the letter of the bishops of the proconsular province to Paul, patriarch of Constantinople, at the Lateran Council, where Felix, bishop of the holy Church of Trisipellis—or, as in the manuscript of Beauvais, Trisipelis—is recorded as subscribing.]

He said: “I am present.”

Felicianus, bishop of the aforesaid place, said: “I recognize him.”

Again he read:

Adeodatus, bishop of the people of Bencenna.

[Note: [Col. 1293D] **Bencennensis.** Perhaps *Beneventensis* or *Benentensis* should be read; this is a see in the proconsular province. Among the African bishops in the subscriptions of the Council of Arles in 314 is found Anastasius, bishop from the city of Beneventum.]

He said: “I am present. It has been Catholic from the beginning.”

Again he read:

Faustinus, bishop of the people of Sillita.

[Note: [Col. 1293D] **Sillitanae.** In the province of Numidia, as the *Notitia*, no. 54, shows.]

[Col. 1293B] He said: “I am present.”

Possidonius, bishop of the aforesaid place, said: “I recognize him.”

Again he read:

Felix, bishop of the people of Aptugna.

[Note: [Col. 1293D] **Aptugnitanae.** Thus it is read everywhere in Augustine. In Optatus and in the acts of the vindication of Autumnus it is commonly *Aptungitanae*.]

He said: “I am present; the whole place is Catholic.”

Again he read:

Geta, bishop of the people of Jubaltiana.

[Note: [Col. 1293D; 1294B] **Jubaltianensis.** In the province of Byzacena, as the *Notitia* shows. Geta, named here as its bishop, attended the Council of Carthage in 403, as is reported in canon 90 of the Code of Canons of the African Church. Restitutus also seems to have been bishop of the same see; in the letter of the bishops of the province of Byzacena he is called bishop of Jubedida, or, in the Beauvais copy, Jubalida.]

He said: “I am present. I have no other man opposed to me.”

Again he read:

[Col. 1294A] Januarius, bishop of the people of Cenculiana.

[Note: [Col. 1294B] **Cenculianensis**, or rather *Cunculianensis*, in the *Notitia* of the province of Byzacena.]

He said: “I am present; there is no other bishop there; it is Catholic.”

Again he read:

Julianus, bishop of the people of Tasfalta. [266]

[Note: [Col. 1294C] **Tasfaltensis.** In the *Notitia* of the same province, Tasbaltensis. At the Council of Carthage under Cyprian, Adelfius of Thasbalte—or, as some manuscripts have it, Thasvalte—gave his judgment. Antoninus, in his *Itinerary*, mentions Tabalta among the cities of Byzacena. At the Council of Cabarsussa in 393, Innocentius of Thebalta subscribed among the Donatist bishops. Perhaps this is the person of whom it is said here: “It is a year since he died.”]

He said: “I am present; there is unity, and the whole place there is Catholic.”

Adeodatus, bishop, said: “It is a year since he died.”

Again he read:

Crescentianus, bishop of the people of Arena.

[Note: [Col. 1294C] **Arenensis.** It is uncertain to which province this belonged.]

He said: “I am present; unity is with me.”

Again he read:

Licentius, bishop of the people of Zattara.

[Note: [Col. 1294C–D] **Zattarensis.** Zattara was a very well-known city of Numidia. Of the four bishops who presented to King Huneric a written declaration of faith, one was Januarius of Zattara, as Victor of Vita testifies, book III. Felix, bishop of Zattara and delegate of Numidia, attended the Council of Carthage under Boniface in 525, and another under Reparatus in 534. We also have Cresconius, bishop of Zattara in the province of Numidia, who attended the Fifth Ecumenical Council. In the *Notitia* of bishops who came to Carthage in the sixth year of King Huneric, Januarius of Jactara is listed among the Numidians; but whether he was different from the Januarius of Zattara mentioned above is uncertain.]

He said: “I am present; it is Catholic there.”

Again he read:

Malcus, bishop of the people of Mascula.

[Note: [Col. 1294D] **Masculitanae.** A city of Numidia; see note 48 to book I of Optatus, p. 15.]

He said: “I am present.”

Vitalis, bishop of the aforesaid place, said: “I recognize him.”

Again he read:

Marianus, bishop of the people of Rufiniana.

[Note: [Col. 1294D] **Rufinianensis.** In the province of Byzacena, as the *Notitia* shows.]

He said: “I am present; he possesses the unity of the Catholic Church.”

Again he read:

Tertiolus, bishop of the people of Cillita.

[Note: [Col. 1294D] **Cillitanae.** In the same province, according to the same *Notitia*.]

He said: “I am present.”

Donatus, bishop of the aforesaid place, said: “I recognize him.”

Again he read:

Sopater, bishop of the people of Tambaia.

[Note: [Col. 1294D] **Tambaiensis.** Of a city in the province of Byzacena, mentioned by Victor of Vita in book V of his work on the Vandal persecution. At the Council of Carthage under Cyprian, Secundianus of Tambaia was present; and among the Donatist bishops, in chapter 44, Gemelius, bishop of Tambaia, subscribes. Among the bishops of the province of Byzacena, the *Notitia* mentions a bishop of Tambeita. Formerly *Tambalensis* was read, but Baluzius corrected it to *Tambaiensis*, because when Faustinus, Sopater’s opponent, is named below, he is called bishop of Tambaia.]

He said: “I am present.”

Faustinus, bishop of the aforesaid place, said: “I recognize him.”

Again he read:

Paulus, [Col. 1295A] bishop of the people of Uzittara.

[Note: [Col. 1295B–C] **Uzittarensis.** In the *Notitia* of the proconsular province there is a bishop of Usita, whose see Baluzius considers identical with this one. Hirtius mentions Usita in Africa in his book on the African War, but that place lay in the province of Byzacena, as Theoderic Ruinart observes after Noris; Hirtius says that it was six Roman miles from the harbor of Lesser Leptis. Leptis, however, was in Byzacena, eighteen Roman miles beyond Hadrumetum toward Tripoli, as Antoninus testifies in his *Itinerary*; consequently it lay too far from the proconsular province to be assigned to it. Ptolemy also supports this conclusion: in book IV, chapter 3, he lists Usita among the cities subject to Hadrumetum.]

He said: “I am present; I have no one from that party.”

Habetdeus, the deacon, said: “He has departed from the body.”

Again he read:

Januarius, bishop of the people of Aptuca.

[Note: [Col. 1295C] **Aptucensis.** Take care not to confuse Aptuca with Aptunga, a city of the proconsular province. Where Aptuca was situated is uncertain.]

Dominicus, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “He is here; he has been affected by bodily illness.”

Again he read:

Victor, bishop of the Church of Utica.

[Note: [Col. 1295C] **Uticensis.** A very well-known city of the proconsular province, famous for Cato’s death, as Pomponius Mela and Pliny observe.]

He said: “I am present.”

Gedulus, bishop of the aforesaid city, said: “I recognize him.”

Again he read:

He who, as stated above, had subscribed for Cericius, bishop of the people of Ucula.

[Note: [Col. 1295C] **He who above for Cericius.** Formerly the reading was: “Again he read: He who above. Procericius, bishop of the people of Ucula.” But Baluzius corrected this passage, and correctly. The meaning is that the Catholic bishop who had just subscribed, namely Victor of Utica, had also subscribed on behalf of Cericius, bishop of the people of Ucula, then absent; but Cericius, now present, approves the subscription and replies.]

[Note: [Col. 1295D] **Uculensis.** It is inferred from the letter of the bishops of this province at the Lateran Council under Martin that this see, distinct from Uzulensis mentioned above in chapter 126, belonged to the proconsular province; Cresconius, bishop of the Church of Ucula, is recorded as subscribing to that letter.]

When he came forward, he said: “I am present; the whole place is Catholic.”

Again he read:

Basilius, bishop of the people of Altibura.

[Note: [Col. 1295D] **Altiburitanae**, or *Altuburitanae*, in the proconsular province, as the *Notitia* shows. Victor, bishop of Altibura, attended the Council of Cabarsussa, and Constantinus, bishop of the Church of Altobura, subscribed to the synodal letter of the proconsular Fathers at the Lateran Council under Martin.]

He said: “I am present.”

Augustialis, bishop of the aforesaid place, said: “I recognize him.”

Again he read:

Victor, bishop of the people of Vina.

[Note: [Col. 1295D; 1296B] **Vinensis.** In the same proconsular province, as is clear from the same synodal letter, to which Fructuosus, bishop of Vina, subscribed. Among the bishops of the Council of Cabarsussa is found Faustinus, the Donatist bishop of Bina; Baluzius thinks him to be the person concerning whom Habetdeus the deacon says here: “We do not have him; he departed from the body five years ago.”]

He said: [Col. 1295B] “I am present.”

Habetdeus, the deacon, said: “We do not have him; he departed from the body five years ago.”

Again he read:

Fructuosus, bishop of the people of Abzirita.

[Note: [Col. 1296B–C] **Abziritensis**, or *Abziritanus*, or *Abderitanus*. For Victor, the bishop who attended the Council of Carthage in 397, is called in the printed texts bishop of Abdera, but in a very ancient manuscript of the Colbert Library, bishop of Abzira. Perhaps Victorianus of Auzira, who subscribed to the synodal letter of the Fathers of the proconsular province at the Lateran Council under Martin, was bishop of this see. Take care, however, not to confuse this see with Abaritana, which is second in the *Notitia* of the proconsular province.]

Vincentius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “He is at Carthage; he has become aware of his condition.”

[Note: [Col. 1296C] **Sensit sibi.** A corrupt passage, from which it may nevertheless be inferred that Fructuosus was unwell.]

Adeodatus, bishop, said: “It is a diocese of Felicianus of Utina; he has a presbyter there.”

[Note: [Col. 1296C] **Utinensis.** In the proconsular province. This Felicianus is also mentioned in chapters 133 and 187.]

Again he read:

Publianus, [Col. 1296A] bishop of the people of Bazarididaca.

[Note: [Col. 1296C] **Bazarididacensis.** It is uncertain to which province this belonged.]

He said: “I am present; there is unity.”

Again he read:

Cassianus, bishop of the people of Bamaccora.

[Note: [Col. 1296C] **Bamaccorensis.** In the *Notitia* of Numidia it is corruptly read *Damatcorensis*. Here, in an old book, *Vamaccorensis*; but in chapter 187, *Bamaccorensis*. Pliny, book V, chapter 4, mentions in Africa the city of Vamacures. At the Council of Carthage under Cyprian occurs Felix of Amaccura or Amachorra, for whom scholars conjecture that *of Bamaccura* should be read.]

He said: “I am present.”

Donatus, bishop of the aforesaid city, said: “I recognize him; he was my presbyter.”

Again he read:

Cresconius, bishop of the people of Zaraita.

[Note: [Col. 1296C] **Zaraitensis**, or *Zarattensis*, in Numidia, as the *Notitia* shows.]

He said: “I am present.”

Rogatus, bishop of the aforesaid place, said: “I recognize him.”

Again he read:

Felix, bishop of Villaregia.

[Note: [Col. 1296C–D] **Villaregensis.** Incorrectly *Villadegensis* in the *Notitia* of Numidia. In chapters 48 and 77 of the Code of Canons of the African Church, Cresconius, bishop of Villaregia in Numidia, is rebuked because, having abandoned his own see, he had seized the Church of Tubia. Augustine, book II against Cresconius, chapter 10, praises Candidus, bishop of Villaregia, a former Donatist made Catholic whose episcopal rank was preserved.]

He said: “I am present; I have no bishop opposed to me. He has only just departed from the body.”

Victor, bishop of the aforesaid place, said: “It is established that I have only just been ordained.”

Again he read:

Primulus, bishop of the people of Tamagris.

[Note: [Col. 1296D] **Tamagristensis.** In Mauretania Sitifensis, as the *Notitia* shows.]

He said: “I am present.”

Saturnius, bishop of the aforesaid city, said: “I recognize him.”

Again he read:

Adeodatus, [Col. 1296B] bishop of the people of Satafa. [267]

[Note: [Col. 1296D] **Satafensis.** There is a Satafa in Sitifensis, no. 6, and another in Caesariensis, no. 116. The bishops mentioned here belonged to one or the other see.]

He said: “I am present.”

Urbanus, bishop of the aforesaid place, said: “I recognize him.”

Again he read:

Faustinianus, bishop of the people of Tamogade.

[Note: [Col. 1296D] **Tamogadensis**, or *Tamugadensis*, in Numidia. See Baluzius’s note on the acts of the vindication of Caecilianus, above, p. 171.]

He said: “I am present.”

Gaudentius, bishop of the aforesaid place, said: “I recognize him.”

Again he read:

Avitus, bishop of the people of Lamasua.

[Note: [Col. 1296D; 1297C] **Lamasuensis.** Likewise in Numidia, as the same *Notitia* shows. Januarius, Avitus’s opponent, is later called, in chapter 187, bishop of Lamasba; and at the Council of Carthage under Cyprian Pusillus of Lamasba gave his judgment. This town is likewise called Lamasba in Antoninus’s *Itinerary*; in the Peutinger Tables, Lamasbua.]

He said: “I am present.”

Januarius, bishop of the aforesaid city, [Col. 1297A] said: “I recognize him.”

Again he read:

Sextilius, bishop of the people of Assaba.

[Note: [Col. 1297C] **Assabensis**, or rather *Assafensis*, in Sitifensis, as the *Notitia* shows.]

He said: “I am present.”

Marcianus, bishop of the aforesaid place, said: “I recognize him.”

Again he read:

Marcianus, bishop of Idicra.

[Note: [Col. 1297C] **Idicrensis.** In Numidia. See note 49 on book II of Optatus, p. 42.]

He said: “I am present.”

Martialis, bishop, said: “I recognize him.”

Again he read:

Crispulus, bishop of the Church of Volita.

[Note: [Col. 1297C–D] **Volitanae.** Ptolemy, among the other cities which in book IV, chapter 3 he states were under Carthage, lists Vol as the second. In the *Notitia* of the proconsular province its bishop is called Bolitanus, and Paulinus, in the *Life of Ambrose*, praises Mauranus, bishop of Bolita. Augustine’s Sermon 13, on the words of the Apostle, was delivered on the feast-day of the Bolitan martyrs; and the commemoration of the holy Volitans is celebrated in the Carthaginian calendar on 17 October, the sixteenth day before the Kalends of November.]

He said: “I am present.”

Quodvultdeus, bishop, said: “I recognize him.”

Again he read:

Germanus, bishop of Gypsaria.

[Note: [Col. 1297D] **Gypsariensis.** In Mauretania Caesariensis, as may be inferred from Ptolemy, book IV, chapter 14. Yet in the Peutinger Tables and in the Anonymous of Ravenna, Gypsaria is located among the towns of the province of Byzacena.]

He said: “I am present.”

Fidentinus, bishop, said: “I recognize him.”

Again he read:

Rogatus, bishop of Gaguarita.

[Note: [Col. 1297D] **Gaguaritanus.** In the *Notitia* of the province of Byzacena he is called Gauvaritanus.]

He said: “I am present; he has unity.”

Adeodatus, bishop, said: “He was ours; he passed over from us to him.”

Again he read:

Quadratus, bishop of the people of Gegita.

[Note: [Col. 1297D] **Gegitanae.** A bishop of Gegita is listed in the *Notitia* of Mauretania Sitifensis. This one is more likely meant than Ziggensis, which is in the proconsular province.]

He said: [Col. 1297B] “I am present; there has never been a bishop there.”

Again he read:

Gregorius, bishop of Tamalla.

[Note: [Col. 1297D] **Tamallensis.** This is Tamalluma of Mauretania Sitifensis.]

He said: “I am present.”

Lucius, bishop, said: “I recognize him.”

Again he read:

Lucius, bishop of the city of Tagara.

[Note: [Col. 1297D] **Tagaratensis.** In the proconsular province, as the *Notitia* shows.]

He said: “I am present.”

Quintus, bishop, said: “I recognize him.”

Again he read:

Felicianus, bishop of the people of Cufruta.

[Note: [Col. 1298C] **Cufrutensis.** In the province of Byzacena, as the *Notitia* shows. This Felicianus attended the Council of Carthage in 403, and there too is called bishop of Cufruta.]

He said: “I am present; I have no other bishop.”

129. Primianus, bishop, said: “The man in question was condemned by us and by them. Though they knew him to be guilty, they too confirmed it. Another has not yet been ordained.”

And in another hand: “I, Primianus, bishop, have verified this.”

Again he read:

Bonifacius, bishop of Cena.

[Note: [Col. 1298C] **Cenensis.** It is uncertain to which province this belonged.]

He said: “I am present.”

Vindemius, bishop, said: “I recognize him.”

Again he read:

Adeodatus, bishop of the people of Bazarita.

[Note: [Col. 1298C] **Bazaritanae.** In Numidia, as the *Notitia* shows. His opponent Calipotius, below in chapter 188, is called Calipodius, bishop of Vazarita.]

He said: [Col. 1297C] “I am present. Calipotius is indeed still alive; but when he saw that the entire people had been converted to the Catholic Church, he departed.”

Again he read:

Niventius, bishop of Tunugaba.

[Note: [Col. 1298C] **Tunugabensis.** It is uncertain to which province this belonged.]

He [Col. 1298A] said: “I am present. I have no bishop there opposed to me.”

130. Primianus, bishop, said: “He was condemned on a charge of adultery; nevertheless he remained there until the present year.”

Again he read:

Sabinus, bishop of Tucca.

[Note: [Col. 1298C] **Tuccensis.** Not Tucca in Sitifensis, nor Tucca in Byzacena, but a town of this name formerly within the diocese of Milevum, as is clear from what follows.]

He said: “I am present.”

Adeodatus, bishop, said: “He was ordained in my diocese; he came from my presbyterate.”

Sabinus, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “Since I was often asked by my fellow citizens to receive them into the communion of the Catholic Church, they asked that a bishop be given to them. They requested me, and I was ordained.”

Adeodatus, bishop, said: “Whom did he have as predecessor? Let him state in whose place he succeeded.”

131. Marcellinus, most illustrious man, tribune and notary, [Col. 1298B] said: “Is it established that there was no Catholic Church there?”

Adeodatus, bishop, said: “No.”

Again he read:

Marianus, bishop of the people of Utzippara.

[Note: [Col. 1298C–D] **Utzipparitanorum.** In the proconsular province, as the *Notitia*, which has a bishop of Uzippara, shows. This Marianus later attended the Council of Carthage in 419.]

He said: “I am present; I have never had another man there.”

Again he read:

Victorius, bishop of the people of Laris.

[Note: [Col. 1298D] **Larensis.** In the proconsular province. Victor of Vita mentions it in book II, no. 6, of his *History of the Vandals*. At the Council of Carthage under Cyprian, Hortensianus of Laris gave his judgment. Vitulus, bishop of the people of Laris, attended the Council of Carthage under Boniface in 525. There was a fortress named Lar in Mauretania Caesariensis, as Antoninus’s *Itinerary* and the Anonymous of Ravenna show, but it was different from the town of Laris mentioned by Victor of Vita. For the latter was near Sicca Veneria, and the bishops were brought there to be transported from that place into the desert. Augustine, in Letter 219 to Count Darius, mentions the towns of Hilaris and Sicca as near neighbors; nor does Hilaris appear to be different from Laris.]

He said: “I am present.”

Honoratus, bishop, said: “I recognize him.”

132. Hilarus, recorder, said: “Since we have filled the codices and other recorders must be substituted for us, let Your Nobility order others from our body to be substituted, with guards assigned to us.”

Vitalius, notary of the Catholic Church, said: “I too submit the same request which the recorder submits to Your Nobility.”

Marcellinus, most illustrious man, tribune and notary, said: “Let guards be assigned, from each party, to the notaries who affirm that they have filled the codices, and to the recorders.”

Aurelius, bishop of the Catholic Church of Carthage, [Col. 1298C] said: “We have already reported, in the mandate itself, that we selected guards. From among them we also offer two guards.”

And in another hand: “I have verified this.”

Marcellinus, most illustrious man, tribune and notary, said: “State the names of those now offered.”

Alypius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “Deuterius—

[Note: [Col. 1299B] **Deuterius.** Bishop of Caesarea in Mauretania, as is clear from Augustine, *Retractations*, book II, chapter 51. BALUZIUS.]

—and Restitutus.”

[Note: [Col. 1299B] **Restitutus.** Bishop of Tagaste in Numidia.]

Marcellinus, most illustrious man, tribune and notary, said: “It is fitting that, just as other recorders have been substituted, so guards should also be provided by the other party.”

Primianus, bishop of Carthage, said: “We provide as guards our colleagues Victor of Hippo—

[Note: [Col. 1299C–D] **Hipponiensem.** Hippo Diarrhytus in the proconsular province, not Hippo Regius in the province of Numidia. For Macrobius, Augustine’s opponent as bishop of Hippo Regius, was not Victor; and in chapter 139 this Victor is called the opponent of Florentinus, bishop of the Catholic Church of Hippo-Zaritus, and finally, explicitly, in chapter 179 he is called bishop of Hippo Diarrhytus. In Ptolemy, book IV, chapter 3, it is called Ἵππον Διάρρυτος, “Hippo Diarrhytus”; Pliny, book V, chapter 4, asserts that the Greeks gave it this name because of its waters flowing through it. It is designated by the same name in Pomponius Mela, book I, chapter 7, on the situation of the world; in Antoninus’s *Itinerary* it is called Hippozarhytus. In the Peutinger Tables, Ipponte Diarito. In the Anonymous of Ravenna, book III, no. 6, Hippone-Zareston; and in book V, no. 5, Yppone Zarestum. Strabo, book XVII, mentions both Hippos, but errs in giving both the name Regius. Solinus, more correctly, distinguishes the two cities in his *Polyhistor*, chapter 30, thus: “Hippo, later called Regius; likewise the other Hippo, called Diarrhytus because of the strait flowing between it and the other—most famous towns founded by Greek horsemen.” At the Council of Carthage under Cyprian, Martyr Petrus of Hippo Diarrhytus delivered his judgment. Augustine, *City of God*, book XVI, chapter 8, calls it Hippo Diarrhytus. Finally, Donatus, “by the grace of God bishop of the holy Church of Hippo-Zaritus,” subscribes to the letter of the proconsular bishops at the Lateran Council.]

—and Marinianus of Oea [268]—

[Note: [Col. 1299D; 1300B] **Oeensem.** In Tripolitania, as the *Notitia* shows. Antoninus, in the *Itinerary*, has Oea; Ptolemy, book IV, chapter 3, Heoa. Pliny calls it the city of Oea. Ammianus Marcellinus, book XXIX, chapter 6, mentions the territory of Oea in the province of Tripolitania. Apuleius is said to have had a statue among the people of Coa in Augustine, Letter 138; but eleven manuscripts read *Ocenses* and five *Oeenses*, and that this is the correct reading is clear from what is immediately added: “from which city he had his wife.” For Pudentilla, Apuleius’s wife, was from Oea, as Apuleius himself testifies in the *Apology*. At the Council of Carthage under Cyprian, Natalis of Oea gave judgment both for himself and for his fellow provincials Pompeius of Sabrata and Dioga of Greater Leptis.]

133. Marcellinus, a *vir clarissimus*, tribune and notary, said: “Since it appears that bishop-guardians have been appointed from both parties, the office must, as it has begun, read aloud the names and subscriptions of each individual; and, for greater care, the vigilance of the guardians on either side shall mark the documents received, so that, when opened in their presence [Col. 1299B], they may be copied and the proceedings preserved in an orderly sequence of written sheets.”

And when the documents from both parties had been received and marked, it was read aloud:

“Innocentius, bishop of Lamiggae [Note: [Col. 1300C] Lamiggae. There are two cities of this name in Africa, both in Numidia: one is no. 101 and the other no. 122 in the *Notitia*. Two Donatist bishops of Lamiggae likewise occur in this Conference: namely, Junianus here and in chapter 198, and Recargentius in chapter 187.], in the presence of Marcellinus, *vir clarissimus*, tribune and notary, I dictated and subscribed the foregoing at Carthage.”

When this had been read, he said: “I am present.”

Bishop Junianus said: “I do not know him, nor does he know me.”

And it was read aloud:

“Rufinianus, bishop of Bonusta [Note: [Col. 1300C] Bonusta. In the proconsular province, as the *Notitia* teaches.], in the presence of Marcellinus, *vir clarissimus*, tribune and notary, I dictated and subscribed the foregoing at Carthage.”

When it had been read, [Col. 1300A] he said: “There have never been Donatists there.”

Primianus, bishop of Carthage, said: “He himself was ours, but we have people for whom to ordain [Note: [Col. 1300C] “For whom to ordain.” Something is lacking here.].”

Rufinianus, bishop of the Catholic Church of Bonusta, said: “It has never had one.”

And it was read aloud:

“Laodicius, bishop of the people of Clypea [Note: [Col. 1300C] Clypea. In the proconsular province, as the *Notitia* teaches. Crescens, bishop of Clypea, attended the Council of Carthage under Boniface in 525; and Stephanus, bishop of the Church of Clypea, subscribed the synodical letter of the bishops of the proconsular province at the Lateran Council under Martin. Clypea is a city celebrated by Ptolemy, Hirtius, Pliny, Pomponius Mela, Solinus, Silius Italicus, Florus, and others. It was the first of all African cities to come under Roman power under Regulus, as Polybius and Florus observe.], in the presence of Marcellinus, *vir clarissimus*, tribune and notary, I dictated and subscribed the foregoing at Carthage.”

When it had been read, he said: “Geminius is on the opposing side.”

And it was read aloud:

“Donatus, bishop of the people of Burita [Note: [Col. 1300D] Burita.
