151. Marcellinus, most distinguished man, tribune and notary, said: “Both the mandate and the subscriptions attached to it shall be entered in the present proceedings. For fuller assurance, however, let each party indicate whether anything concerning the reciprocal mandates is disputed.”

152. Aurelius, bishop of the Catholic Church of Carthage, [Col. 1321B] said: “In accordance with the subscriptions to the mandate, our men came forward one by one and declared that they had authorized us. Let these men do the same: after the subscriptions have been read, let each of them declare that he gave authorization and subscribed to this mandate.” And in another hand: “I have verified it.”

153. Marcellinus, most distinguished man, tribune and notary, said: “They were ordered to come forward one by one so that their presence, not their declaration, might be established. For no one disputes that the subscriptions alone can suffice. The question now, therefore, is whether the mandates of both parties appear acceptable to both parties.”

154. Aurelius, bishop of the Catholic Church of Carthage, said: “But we wish them to answer for their subscriptions. By your well-being, let them acknowledge that they gave authorization, since your Highness was not present when these men subscribed. What they did secretly, let them declare publicly.” And in another hand: “I have verified it.”

155. Marcellinus, most distinguished man, tribune and notary, said: “The request is fair, although it is certain that the subscriptions can suffice.”

156. Aurelius, bishop of the Catholic Church of Carthage, said: “They themselves have made us more cautious.”

157. Rufinianus the clerk read: “Januarianus, bishop of the Casenses [Nigrenses].” When he had read it, Januarianus, bishop, said: “I both authorized and subscribed. Let it therefore be written that I have no adversary from their party among my people.”

Rufinianus the clerk read: “Primianus, bishop of Carthage.” When he had read it, Primianus, bishop of Carthage, [Col. 1321D] said: “I had given authorization; but I received this mandate.”

Rufinianus the clerk read: “Felix, bishop of the city of Rome.” When he had read it, Felix, bishop of the city [Col. 1322A] of Rome, said: “I both authorized and subscribed.”

Possidius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “Where is Felix?” And in another hand: “I have verified it.”

158. Aurelius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “Granted that he calls himself bishop of the city of Rome. Why is prejudice being caused to the absent man?”

[Note: *To the absent man:* that is, to the true bishop of Rome, who at that time was Innocent. — Baluzius.]

And in another hand: “I have verified it.”

159. Petilianus, bishop, said: “No one is ignorant what circumstance brought him here.”

[Note: *What circumstance:* namely, the disaster of the city of Rome, which Alaric, king of the Goths, had captured on the ninth day before the Kalends of September in the preceding year. — Baluzius.]

“You yourselves know that all the Roman nobility is here. The same tempest, therefore, and the same necessity brought him here. So that he might not seem to dissent from us, he too gave authorization.” And in another hand: “I, Petilianus, bishop, have verified it.”

160. Aurelius, bishop of the Catholic Church of Carthage, said: “We too could have brought in persons from overseas [Col. 1322B] whose names we might add to the mandate.” And in another hand: “I have verified it.”

161. Marcellinus, most distinguished man, tribune and notary, said: “Although your Holiness may more fully acknowledge that I have been defined by imperial authority as having jurisdiction only among the bishops of the African provinces, nevertheless, without prejudice to the bishop of the city of Rome, I gladly permit even this, though it is superfluous.”

162. Aurelius, bishop of the Catholic Church of Carthage, said: “It is enough that we have not prejudiced the absent man.” In another hand: “I have verified it.”

163. Petilianus, bishop, said: “Let them follow and maintain this point in every respect: that they will say nothing on behalf of absentees and persons overseas.” And in another hand: “I, Petilianus, [Col. 1322C] bishop, have verified it.”

Aurelius, bishop of the Catholic Church of Carthage, said: “It is enough that we have said that Innocent is bishop of the city of Rome.” And in another hand: “I have verified it.”

Rufinianus the clerk read: “Donatus, bishop of Botriana.” The same man said: “I both authorized and subscribed. Let it be written that I have no opponent.”

Rufinianus the clerk read: “Florianus, bishop of Putiza.” When he had read it, Primianus, bishop of Carthage, said: “He fell ill here at Carthage. Fearing his end, he departed; he had already subscribed.”

And he read: “Candorius, bishop of Aggerita.” When he had read it, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed. I have an opponent.”

And he read: “Antonius, bishop of Lamsorta.” The same man said: “I authorized and subscribed. I have no adversary there.”

And he read: “Datianus, bishop of Tamica.”

[Note: *Tamicensis,* not *Timicensis.* For the Donatist bishop of the latter place was named Optatus, as is clear from the preceding material; but perhaps this is Tamazucensis or Tamazensis, listed in the Notitia of Mauretania Caesariensis, no. 120. There is also a bishop of Tamazena among the Byzacenes, Victorianus, mentioned in the letter reported at the Lateran Council under Martin; he has no mention in the Notitia.]

The same man said: “I authorized and [Col. 1322D] subscribed; I have no adversary there.”

And he read: “Victorianus, bishop of Abissa.”

[Note: *Abissensis:* it is unknown in which province this see lay.]

When he had read it, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed; I [Col. 1323A] have an adversary in my diocese.”

And he read: “Natalicus, bishop of Zella.” When he had read it, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Maximinus, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “It is the diocese of Bishop Mizonius.”

[Note: *Of Bishop Mizonius:* earlier, near the end of chapter 135, it is not Mizonius but Donatianus who is called the Catholic bishop against whom Natalicus of Zella stood. Baluzius therefore suspects that the name of some Donatist bishop, whose adversary was this Mizonius, has dropped out here; unless one says that there were two bishops in the diocese of Zella, Donatianus and Mizonius.]

“He has presbyters and a more numerous people than he.”

And he read: “Fortis, bishop of Cedia.” When he had read it, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed; I have no adversary.”

164. Marcellinus, most distinguished man, tribune and notary, said: “Since it would take a long time to go through them one by one, let these ten, who have declared that they gave authorization, state for the record whether all the subscriptions were made in their presence, and let them give their agreement to what has been done.”

165. Petilianus, bishop, said: “Your Magnificence, noble sir, is indeed using a considerable expedient: the ten fathers and colleagues of ours who have already declared that they gave authorization [Col. 1323B] and subscribed are to attest that all the other fathers also subscribed. To be sure, this greatly serves that purpose: that the time of this day may not be prolonged further. Yet it is useful to the case that each person declare both that he authorized and that he subscribed, so that they may also not be silent about the fact that they have no rivals.

“For it seems to profit those who have shown that they have many opponents against our people throughout this province, if we do not show that in the province of Numidia they have none at all—or at least have them only in rare places. For our whole contention, noble sir, as you deign to remember, has very often turned upon number and clings to that point most strongly. And although peace nourishes and preserves our multitude, whereas wars procure a multitude for them, since, while we are absent, they set up many figures everywhere—in districts, cities, and dioceses—so as to seem numerous…”

[Note: *Figures:* that is, bishops set up as mere personae.]

“…nevertheless, even if the number on each side were equal, mine ought to seem greater, because it remained standing even while I was absent, and because it is original and authentic and is not surpassed by multiplied rivalry.” And in another hand: “I, Petilianus, bishop, have verified it.”

166. Marcellinus, most distinguished man, tribune and notary, said: “I wished to satisfy your desire in investigating everything. But it is established that no inquiry concerning numbers was entrusted to me.”

167. Petilianus, bishop, said: “Let what we ought not to have passed over be preserved for us.”

[Col. 1323D]

168. Fortunatianus, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “We could indeed have shown in Africa a greater number belonging to the Catholic Church spread throughout the whole world, insofar as the case is concerned, if the whole weight of the proceeding rested on this. But since the very grave Petilianus employs certain delaying tactics, let superfluities be cut away and the case now proceed to its beginning. We make known and represent to your Nobility that he wished, through his presentation, to draw forth an empty prejudice against us.” And while he was speaking: “And in another hand: I have verified it.”

169. Petilianus, bishop, said: “You are making an empty accusation; it shall be repaid to you; and although repayment ought not to be made, keep it to yourself.” And in another hand: “I have verified it.”

170. Fortunatianus, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “In saying this, he put forward the little snares of an excuse: that before the day of hearing he had allegedly observed the bishops of the Donatist party, as though a senate of heaven, exhausted by prolonged labour; whereas a hearing has always been sought altogether by our party. But we observed the appointed day and time for this reason: that in this also the obedience of the Catholic Church might be shown.” And while he was speaking: “And in another hand: I have verified it.”

171. Marcellinus, most distinguished man, tribune and notary, [Col. 1324B] said: “In accordance with the tenor of the edict, both parties must conduct the case with only those remaining at this hearing for whom it has been established that the jurisdiction was entrusted by all, in accordance with their declarations.”

172. Fortunatianus, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “In order that the case may be heard, let your Highness order the superfluous crowd surrounding us to withdraw.” And in another hand: “I have verified it.”

173. Marcellinus, most distinguished man, tribune and notary, said: “This must be done. But first, the ten from each party must acknowledge that they agreed upon the persons of the subscribers; and although their presence was secured at your request, nevertheless, lest anything appear to have been denied you, let the subscriptions of all be read aloud in order.”

[Col. 1324C]

174. Alypius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “Let them answer whether the subscriptions of all which are contained in the mandate were written here at Carthage.” And in another hand: “I have verified it.”

175. Emeritus, bishop, said: “So far as I have understood from the presentation, it was necessary that a declaration be obtained from our side. The patience of your judicial proceedings, which gives everyone an opportunity, gladly assented that those who subscribed should also insert their declaration into the proceedings by their present confirmation. We ask your Excellency that, when the subscription begins to be read, you deign to hear those same men.” And in another hand: “I, Emeritus, have verified it.”

176. Marcellinus, most distinguished man, tribune and notary, said: “Let all the subscriptions be read aloud, as I ordered.”

Rufinianus the clerk read: “Optatus, bishop [Col. 1324D] of Rusuccuru.” When he had read it, Optatus, bishop, said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

And he read: “Pomponius, bishop of Macriana.” When he had read it, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

And he read: “Donatianus, bishop of Bagaia.” When he had read it, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

And he read: “Privatus, bishop of Auzaga.”

[Note: *Auzagensis:* there are two Auzagas, as is clear from chapter 179 below. Primulus, bishop of Vaga, of the Donatist party and formerly an opponent of Ampelius—but one who had returned to the Church, as is shortly stated—opposes him. This came about because Africans pronounced the name of this town *Ausvagensis*, [Col. 1325C] as at the Council of Carthage under Cyprian, where Aimnius “of Ausvaga” occurs. Thus, because the first syllable was not heard, they believed him to be of Vaga, [Col. 1325D] and consequently bishops of Vaga opposed him. But just as Vaga was in Numidia, so also was Ausvaga.]

When he had read it, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed; I have no adversary among [Col. 1325A] my people.”

Ampelius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “Recognizing perfect unity from his conversion, my brother Bishop Primulus speaks the most correct faith with me. For he was then a bishop of the Donatist party. Now, having converted, he shows by his conversion that he and his people hold the whole faith. Unity there is complete, not only in the city itself but also in all the dioceses.”

177. Aurelius, bishop of the Catholic Church of Carthage, said: “We ask that the names which he recently read from the subscription be read aloud: I mean Donatianus of Bagaia and Privatus of Vaga.” And in another hand: “I have verified it.”

Marcellinus, most distinguished man, tribune and notary, said: “Let these names, concerning which doubt has arisen, [Col. 1325B] be read again.”

And he read: “Donatianus, bishop of Bagaia; Privatus, bishop of Vaga.”

Alypius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “Far be deceit.”

Rogatus, bishop, said: “It says Januarianus, not Privatus.”

178. Marcellinus, most distinguished man, tribune and notary, said: “But you recognize that it is the same face.”

179. Rogatus, bishop, said: “I know Januarianus; I do not know Privatus.”

Primianus, bishop of Carthage, said: “The matter was previously about two persons. Therefore neither they nor our people have lied. There is one Auzaga where Januarianus was, and he is now dead; there is another Auzaga where Privatus is, and he is now alive.” And in another hand: “I, Primianus, bishop, have verified it.”

180. Marcellinus, most distinguished man, tribune and notary, [Col. 1325C] said: “You have graciously explained to the court, with sufficient episcopal truthfulness, the matter in which error had arisen. Therefore let the rest now be read through.”

And he read: “Donatus, bishop of the people of Celerina.”

[Note: *Celerinensis:* it is uncertain in which province this see lay.]

When he had read it, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed. I have had no adversary at all and have none among my people.”

And he read: “Victor, bishop of Hippo Diarrhytus.” When he had read it, the same man said: “I both authorized and subscribed.”

And he read: “Sarmentius, bishop of Ternamusa.”

[Note: *Ternamusensis:* the old manuscript has *Cernamusensis*, but Baluzius corrected it to *Ternamusensis* from the Antonine Itinerary, where Taranamusa Castra is listed among the towns of Mauretania Caesariensis. Certainly this see differs from Ceramusa in Numidia, which had no Donatist bishop, as stated above in chapter 133. In the Notitia of Mauretania Caesariensis the see is called Ternamunensis; it should be read *Ternamusensis*.]

When he had read it, the same man said: “I both authorized and subscribed. Let the proceedings record that I have no adversary among my people.”

And he read: “Perseverantius, [Col. 1326A] bishop of Theveste.”

[Note: *Tevestinus:* see what we have said on Note 44 in Book II of Optatus.]

When he had read it, the same man said: “I both authorized and subscribed.”

And he read: “Pancratius, bishop of Badia.” When he had read it, the same man said: “I both authorized and subscribed.”

And he read: “Maximianus, bishop of Serteita.”

[Note: *Serteitanus:* in Mauretania Sitifensis, as the Notitia, no. 28, shows.]

When he had read it, the same man said: “I both authorized and subscribed.”

And he read: “Severinus, bishop of Castellum.”

[Note: *Castellanus:* in Mauretania Caesariensis, as the Notitia, no. 75, shows. The Anonymous Ravennate, Book III, no. 8, mentions Castellum among the cities of Mauretania Caesariensis. [Col. 1326C]]

When he had read it, the same man said: “I both authorized and subscribed.”

And he read: “Colonicus, bishop of Tinisa.”

[Note: *Tinistensis,* or *Tinisensis:* perhaps in Numidia. At the Council of Carthage under Cyprian, Venantius of Tinisa gave an opinion. Ptolemy, Book IV, chapter 3, mentions Tinissa.]

When he had read it, the same man said: “I both authorized and subscribed, and I have no traditores in my district.”

And he read: “Felix, bishop of Mopta.” When he had read it, the same man said: “I both authorized and subscribed.”

And he read: “Secundinus, bishop of Jucundiana.”

[Note: *Secundinus, bishop of Jucundiana:* at the Council of Cabarsussi he is called Secundus of Jocundiana, a certain estate in Numidia.]

When he had read it, the same man said: “I both authorized and subscribed; I have no adversaries in the Church.” [Col. 1326B]

And he read: “Donatus, bishop of Vageata.”

[Note: *Vageatensis:* bishop of an estate or village in Numidia, as Alypius immediately argues.]

When he had read it, the same man said: “I both authorized and subscribed.”

181. Alypius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “Let it be written that all these men have been ordained bishops in villages or on estates, not in any cities.” [And in another hand: “I have verified it.”]

182. Petilianus, bishop, said: “So you too have many scattered throughout all the countryside. Indeed, where you have them frequently, you also have them without people.” And in another hand: “I, Petilianus, bishop, have verified it.”

Marcellinus, most distinguished man, tribune and notary, said: “Let what appears to have been represented to the court by both parties be recorded.”

And he read: “Rogatianus, bishop of Idassa.”

[Note: *Idassensis:* in Numidia, as the Notitia, no. 27, shows. From this passage it is inferred that it was not far from Macomadia, since the bishop of Macomadia says that he has a presbyter there.]

When he had read it, the same man said: “I both authorized and subscribed; [Col. 1326C] I have no adversary.”

Aurelius, bishop of the Catholic Church of Macomadia, said: “I have Florentinus, a presbyter, in the Church. There were three Catholic bishops, who have now died; we have not yet been able to ordain another. We have the presbyter Florentinus there.”

And he read: “Germanus, bishop of Zugabbara.” When he had read it, the same man said: “I both authorized and subscribed.”

And he read: “Rogatianus, bishop of Villa Magna.” When he had read it, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed; I have no adversary.”

[Note: *I have no adversary:* earlier, in chapter 133, Augendus said that he was bishop of Villa Magna. Thus either they did not know one another, or they were bishops of distinct sees having the same name.]

And he read: “The presbyter Manilius of Bazium, on behalf of my bishop.”

[Note: *Bazienus,* or *Bazitensis:* in Numidia. For, as is clear from chapter 133, Lucidus was bishop of the people of Marcelliana and Bazium.]

When he had read it:

[Col. 1327A]

183. Marcellinus, most distinguished man, tribune and notary, said: “On behalf of which bishop?”

Petilianus, bishop, said: “He has lost his sight.” And in another hand: “I, Petilianus, bishop, have verified it.”

Alypius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “Let it be answered whether the man on whose behalf he subscribed is present.” And in another hand: “I have verified it.”

Primianus, bishop, said: “Let us speak the truth. He has lost his sight; he could not come, and he sent his presbyter.” And in another hand: “I, Primianus, bishop, have verified it.”

Marcellinus, most distinguished man, tribune and notary, said: “But his name itself ought to have appeared in the subscription.”

184. Alypius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “Let it be attested that they wish to insert even the names of absentees, so that we too may be permitted to insert in the proceedings all Catholic bishops who were unable to be present through illness or some other circumstance.” [Col. 1327B] And in another hand: “I have verified it.”

And he read: “Donatus, bishop of Apissa.”

[Note: *Apissanensis:* it seems that the reading should be “of Pissa” or “of Pesana.” Pesana is counted among the cities of Byzacena in the old Notitia published by Beveridge.]

When he had read it, the same man said: “I both authorized and subscribed; I have no adversary.”

185. Petilianus, bishop, said: “Since the presentation of the opposing party has declared that they have some men absent, we too do not keep silent that some of our own were prevented from coming by many necessities or adverse illnesses, and that certain episcopal seats are now vacant, for which bishops have not yet been ordained. Let the proceedings contain this also.” And in another hand: “I, Petilianus, bishop, have verified it.”

186. Marcellinus, most distinguished man, tribune and notary, said: “As regards confirmation of the mandate, the number of clergy on each side shown to have subscribed to the same mandate is sufficient. Therefore let the rest be read through, setting aside the superfluous excuses concerning absentees.”

And he read: “Quintasius, bishop of Vaiana.” When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

187. Alypius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “Then let the subscription of absentees be erased.” And in another hand: “I have verified it.”

And he read: “Januarius, bishop of Lamasba.” When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Felix, bishop of Novasinna.” When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Martialis, bishop of Idicra.” When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and [Col. 1327D] subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Gedudus, bishop of Utica.” When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and [Col. 1328A] subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Urbanus, bishop of Satafa.” When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Donatus, bishop of Cillita.” When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Liberalis, bishop of the place called Nasae.”

[Note: *Nasaitensis:* it is uncertain in which province this place lay.]

When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed; I neither have had an adversary, nor have one, nor shall have one, God permitting.”

Likewise he read: “Maximianus, bishop of Hermiana.” When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Fortunatus, bishop of Vescerita.” When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Peregrinus, bishop of Sufeta.” When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Donatus, bishop of Merferebita.”

[Note: *Merferebitanus:* it is uncertain in which province this see lay.]

[Col. 1328B] When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Gavinus, bishop of Vegesela.” When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Veratianus, bishop of Carpita.” When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed; I am the successor of Faustinianus, who had been ordained in the unity of truth by Donatus; but later, in the times of Macarius, traditores arose there.”

Likewise he read: “Gaianus, bishop of Tiguala.” When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Rogatus, bishop of Perdica.” When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Victorinus, bishop of the people of Leptiminus.” When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Martinianus, bishop of the place called Tibuzabeta.” [Col. 1328C]

[Note: *Tibuzabetensis:* it is uncertain in which province this place lay.]

When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Quintianus, bishop of Lacus Dulcis.”

[Note: *A Lacu-dulce:* it is uncertain in which province this place lay.]

Valentinianus, deacon of Bishop Primianus, said: “He is ill.”

Likewise he read: “Pelagius, bishop of Vanariona.”

[Note: *Vanarionensis:* perhaps Panatoriana, in Mauretania Caesariensis, as the Notitia, no. 11, shows.]

When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed; I have no adversary.”

Likewise he read: “Victorianus, bishop of Tibarita.” When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Primulianus, bishop of Mandasumita.”

[Note: *Mandasumitanus:* in the province of Byzacena, as the Notitia, [Col. 1328D] no. 110, shows, where he is called Madassumitanus.]

When he came forward, the same man said: “I agreed and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Fortunatianus, bishop of Meta.” When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Felicianus, bishop of Utina.” When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: [Col. 1328D] “Florentinus, bishop of Tubusubtus.”

[Note: *A Tubusubtu:* in the Notitia of Mauretania Sitifensis, no. 8, occurs a bishop called *Tugusubditanus*, for which one should read *Tubusubditanus*. In the Notitia Dignitatum, section 20, appears the *Praepositus limitis Tubusubditani*, “commander of the Tubusubditan frontier.” Ancient writers called it Tubusuptum, and it is so read in Ptolemy, Book IV, chapter 2; Pliny, Book V, chapter 2; the Antonine Itinerary; and Ammianus Marcellinus, Book XXIX, chapter 5. In the Antonine Itinerary it is listed as situated near Saldae, and in the cited passage of Ammianus Tubusuptum is said to have bordered Montiferratus, which, as is clear from the Peutinger Tables, extended from Rusuccuru to the colony of Saldae.]

When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Likewise [Col. 1329A] he read: “Marcus, bishop of Midica.”

[Note: *Midicensis:* a see near Taprura in the province of Byzacena.]

When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed; I have no adversary.”

Alypius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “Where are you from? What is your city?”

Marcus, bishop, said: “Midica lies beside Taprura. Dimenianus of Taprura knows me.”

Likewise he read: “Donatus, bishop of Cresima.”

[Note: *Cresimensis:* it is uncertain in which province this see lay.]

When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed; I have no adversary.”

Likewise he read: “Victorianus, bishop of Puppita.” When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Dativus, bishop of Nova Petra.”

[Note: *Novapetrensis:* a fortified place in Numidia.]

When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed; and I have no adversary, because Lord Marculus is there, whose blood God will exact on the day of judgment.”

Likewise he read: “Maximinus, [Col. 1329B] bishop, said.”

[Note: *Said:* in place of this word, *said,* the name of the town of which Maximinus was bishop ought to be supplied.]

When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Cresconius, bishop of Lega.” When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed; I have neither had nor have an adversary there.”

Likewise he read: “Valentinianus, bishop of Junca.”

[Note: *Juncensis:* in Byzacena, as the Notitia, no. 105, shows. A notable council was held at Junca in 524; Ferrandus cites its canon in the *Breviatio Canonum*, canon 26. The Juncan shore is mentioned in the *Life of Fulgentius.* There was also a bishop of Janca in Mauretania Caesariensis, who appears first in the Notitia of that province. In the letter of the bishops of Byzacena, Numidius, bishop of the holy Church of Sosiana-Junca, subscribes.]

When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Gaudentius, bishop of Zerta.”

[Note: *Zertensis:* see what we have said on chapter 135.]

When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed; I have no adversary.”

Aurelius, bishop of the Catholic Church of Macomasa, said: “There is a Catholic presbyter there.”

Gaudentius, bishop, said: “I have no adversary among my people.”

Likewise he read: “Bonifacius, bishop of Urugita.”

[Note: *Urugitanus:* perhaps Uracita or Urcita, in the proconsular province.]

When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Donatus, bishop [Col. 1329C] of Bamaccora.” When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed, and I have no adversary among my people except Absalom alone.”

[Note: *Absalom:* namely Cassianus, who had been his presbyter, as stated above in chapter 128. For that reason he calls him Absalom here.]

Aurelius, bishop of the Catholic Church of Macomadia, said: “This Cassianus is the bishop present here.”

Likewise he read: “Restitutus, bishop of Drusiliana.” When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: [Col. 1330A] “Flavianus, bishop of Pauzera.”

[Note: *Pauzerensis:* it is uncertain in which province this see lay.]

When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Clarentius, bishop of Tabraca.” When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Recargentius, bishop of Lamiggiga.” When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed; I have no adversary.”

Aurelius, bishop of Macomadia, said: “Crescentianus, a presbyter, is there.”

Likewise he read: “Pascasius, bishop of Tugga.”

[Note: *Tuggensis:* perhaps in the proconsular province. For Victor, bishop of the municipality of Togia, subscribed to the letter of the bishops of the proconsular province at the Lateran Council.]

When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Castus, bishop of Cella.” When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Aptus, bishop of Tuzura.” When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Victor, bishop of Rotaria.” [Col. 1330B]

[Note: *Rotariensis:* in Optatus, Book I, no. 14, p. 15, Felix of Rotaria is listed among the Numidian bishops who attended the Council of Cirta.]

When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed; I have no adversary.”

Aurelius, bishop of the Catholic Church of Macomadia, said: “We had a bishop there. You killed him and seized possession.”

188. Adeodatus, bishop, said: “He says that a bishop was killed. Let him accuse, demonstrate, and press the charge.” And in another hand: “I, Adeodatus, bishop, have verified it.”

Aurelius, bishop of the Catholic Church of Macomadia, said: “And they rebaptized that ninety-year-old man, a bishop.”

[Note: *A ninety-year-old bishop:* namely Simplicius of Tibilis, as is stated at the end of chapter 197.]

Victor, bishop of Azura, [Col. 1330C] of the Catholic Church, said: “He says that he has none. I have a church there, as you well know.”

[Note: *Azurensis:* this Victor is called Ajurensis in Conference II, chapter 15. It is likely that he was from Numidia, since he says that he has a church in the Numidian town of Rotaria.]

Likewise he read: “Calipodius, bishop of Vazaria.” When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Benenatus, bishop of the Casenses Bastalenses.”

[Note: *Casensium Bastalensium:* it is uncertain in which province this see lay.]

[Col. 1330C] [When he came forward, the same man said:] “I authorized and subscribed, and I have no adversary.”

Likewise he read: “Honoratus, bishop of Adquesira.”

[Note: *Adquesirensis:* in Mauretania Caesariensis, as the Notitia, no. 66, shows.]

When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Felix, bishop of Maxula.”

[Note: *Maxulitanus:* in the proconsular province, as the Notitia, no. 30, shows. Maxula is mentioned by Ptolemy, Pliny, the Antonine Itinerary, and the Peutinger Tables. Numidius of Maxula, Felix’s opponent, attended the Council of Carthage under Aurelius in 419, as chapter 112 shows. Another bishop of Maxula bearing the same name subscribed to the Council of Carthage under Boniface in 525. The feast of the saints of Maxula was celebrated on the eleventh day before the Kalends of August in the old Carthaginian Calendar; and we possess two sermons of St. Augustine concerning them, entitled “On the holy Massylitan martyrs.”]

When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Marcianus, bishop of Sitifis.” When he came forward, [Col. 1331A] the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Januarius, bishop of Numidia.”

[Note: *Numidiensis,* or *Numidensis:* in Mauretania Caesariensis, as is immediately stated and as the Notitia of that province, no. 118, shows. This bishopric had been detached from that of Sufasar, as Reparatus complains immediately afterward.]

When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed, and I have no traditores.”

Fortunatianus, bishop of the Catholic Church of Sicca, said: “Where are you from?”

Januarius, bishop, said: “It is Numidia; it is Mauretania Caesariensis.”

Reparatus, bishop of the Catholic Church of Sufasar, said: “It is my diocese. I have a presbyter there; he kept vigil there with you.”

Likewise he read: “Campanus, bishop of Cincarita.” When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Cresconius, bishop of Caesaria.” When he came forward, the same man said: “I authorized and subscribed; I have no rival.”

189. Novatus, bishop of the Catholic Church of Sitifis, said: “He has against him a Catholic presbyter, [Col. 1331B] numerous clerics, and people from the Donatist body. Here in this city of Carthage there is a presbyter and deacon whom he plundered, tortured, and hanged. He plundered the Catholic Church, took away its money, carried off its grain, and drove away its carts, so that this man may know that there is a Catholic Church there. This is what I have pursued.” Adeodatus the bishop said: “All these matters must be handled by documentary evidence. Let the man who asserts a falsehood in a judicial proceeding bear the risk.” And in another hand: “I, Adeodatus, have verified it.” Novatus, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “Order that the presbyter of the place be admitted.”

190. Marcellinus, most distinguished man, tribune and notary, said: “These matters do not pertain to the present inquiry. Let the subscription of the remaining persons, which has been entrusted to me, [Col. 1331C] be read.” Salvianus the bishop [Note: [Col. 1331D] Salvianus the bishop: the bishop of Lepcis, who is named below in chapter 207.] said: “It was prescribed to us long ago what they were to say. The issue concerns bishops, not presbyters.”

191. Fortunatianus, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “Our side replies for this reason: because the Catholic Church is denied there. The present proceedings, which speak for themselves, will show that satisfaction has been given to your impudence.” And in another hand: “I have verified it.”

192. Adeodatus the bishop said: “We thank you, because you always commit an outrage.” And in another hand: “I, Adeodatus, have verified it.”

193. Marcellinus, most distinguished man, tribune and notary, said: “Let these matters be reserved for another time; for the present let what has been referred to the sacred tribunal be carried out.” Then he read:

“Felicissimus, bishop of Obba” [Note: [Col. 1331D] Obba, or Obbitanum, in Mauretania Caesariensis, as is clear from the list of this province, no. 56. Among the bishops present at the Council of Carthage under Cyprian is listed Paul, confessor, from Obba; in certain manuscripts and in Augustine, from Bobba. Pliny places the colony of Bobba in Mauretania. Valerian, bishop of the African Church of Obba, was present at the Fifth Ecumenical Council.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Rufinus, presbyter, signed on behalf of my bishop Julianus of Midila” [Note: [Col. 1331D] Midila, or Midilum. In Numidia, as the list, no. 41, indicates. At the Council of Carthage under Cyprian there was present Jader of Midila, confessor and martyr.]

194. Fortunatianus, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “Let it be answered whether he signed on behalf of one who was present.” And in another hand: “I have verified it.”

195. Adeodatus the bishop said: “Julianus is prevented by illness; but, lest he should appear to have been absent in any respect, he sent a presbyter through whom he might excuse his absence, and the presbyter himself signed for him.” And in another hand: “I have verified it.”

196. Marcellinus, most distinguished man, tribune and notary, said: “The excuse is credible and reasonable.”

197. Fortunatianus, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “We also wish it to be recorded that he signed on behalf of [Col. 1332B] one who was absent.” And in another hand: “I have verified it.”

Then he read: “Optatus, bishop of Timicita.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Victorianus, bishop of Tigimma.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Honorius, bishop of Vartana” [Note: [Col. 1332D] Vartana. The Peutinger Table has Vatari between Flavia Marciana and Velesim. Whether this is the same place as the present one is uncertain.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Martinus, bishop of Siccesita” [Note: [Col. 1332D] Siccesita. In Mauretania Caesariensis, as the list, no. 80, indicates.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Vindemius, bishop from Cenis.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Donatus, bishop of Tanuda” [Note: [Col. 1332D] Tanuda. Perhaps Tamada in Mauretania Caesariensis, from the same list, no. 100.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Possidius, bishop of Sillita.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

[Col. 1332C] Then he read: “Reparatus, bishop of Aquae.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Honoratus, bishop of Lara.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Proficentius, bishop of Macomadia.” When he came forward, he said the same: “Although I have no opponent, I gave instructions and signed.”

Fortunatianus, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “From which Macomadia?” [Note: [Col. 1332D] From which Macomadia? As we observed in chapter 116, there were two Macomadias: one in Numidia, the other in Byzacena. The Proficentius in question was bishop of Macomadia in Byzacena, which was surnamed Rusticiana.]

Proficentius the bishop said: “Rusticiana.”

Then he read: “Paschasius, bishop of Dusis” [Note: [Col. 1332D] Dusis. There follows another bishop with an almost identical name, of Drusis; and in the following chapter, Bebianus, bishop of Dusis. In the list we have no other place of similar name besides Durus in Byzacena.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Antonianus, bishop of Drusis.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Januarius, bishop of Aquae Albae” [Note: [Col. 1332D] Aquae Albae. The list contains two sees of Aquae Albae: one in Byzacena, no. 52, and the other in Mauretania [Col. 1333C] Sitifensis, no. 5. It is uncertain of which Julianus was bishop.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave [Col. 1333A] instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Crescens, bishop of Icosium” [Note: [Col. 1333C] Icosium. In Mauretania Caesariensis, as the list, no. 59, indicates. Icosium was a famous city, granted Latin rights by Vespasian, as Pliny writes. It is mentioned by Ptolemy, Pomponius Mela, Antoninus, Ammianus Marcellinus, and the Anonymous Ravennate. Laurentius of Icosium, bishop of that city and legate of Mauretania Caesariensis, attended the Council of Carthage in 419.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Paschasius, bishop of Tura” [Note: [Col. 1333C] Tura. Mention has already been made of two different bishoprics of Tura; now a third is added, though its province is uncertain. At the Council of Carthage in 525, under Boniface, Felix, bishop of Vicus Turrensis, was present; it is uncertain which of these sees he held.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Victor, bishop of Orre” [Note: [Col. 1333C] Orre, or Horre. Besides Horrea Aninicensis, there was in Mauretania Sitifensis another Horrea, between Sitifis and Tubusuptus, in the Peutinger Table; perhaps this bishop belonged to that place.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Marcianus, bishop of Tabazaga” [Note: [Col. 1333D] Tabazaga. This bishop is above called bishop of Tabaicensis; in the list of Mauretania Caesariensis, Tabadcarensis, no. 103.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Cresconius, bishop of Siguitum” [Note: [Col. 1333D] Siguitum, or Siguitanum. In Numidia, where Sigus is located in the Peutinger Table near Tigisis and Cirta. In Antoninus’s Itinerary it is called Sugus, twenty-five Roman miles from Cirta. There was also a colony named Siga in Mauretania Caesariensis, according to Ptolemy, book V, chapter 2. But Cresconius was bishop in Numidia, for he signs on behalf of Gaudentius, bishop of Tigisis.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed. As I have no opponent, so may I never have one.”

Then he read: “Dativus, bishop of Vise” [Note: [Col. 1333D] Vise. Its province is uncertain.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Quodvultdeus, 282 bishop of Nebbita” [Col. 1333B] [Note: [Col. 1333D] Nebbita. Perhaps Neptis in Byzacena, as the list, no. 14, indicates.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Constantius, bishop of Rusubiccaria” [Note: [Col. 1333D] Rusubiccaria. In the list of Mauretania Caesariensis, no. 22 has Rusuburitanus, and no. 77 Rubicariensis, for which learned men conjecture that Rusubicariensis should be read. Rusubricari appears in Antoninus’s Itinerary and the Peutinger Table. [Col. 1334C] Ptolemy has Rusubeser, book IV, chapter 2, and Rusicibar in the following chapter.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Augustalis, bishop of Altiburum.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Saturninus, bishop of Tamagrista.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Simplicius, bishop of Tibilis” [Note: [Col. 1334C] Tibilis. In Numidia, as the list, no. 66, indicates. See what we said in note 50 on book I of Optatus. For even if Aquae Tibilitanae were distinct from Tibili, as seems likely from the Peutinger Table, both places nevertheless belonged to the same diocese.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed; I have no opponent.”

Aurelius, bishop of the Catholic Church of Macomadia, said: “He is the bishop who was rebaptized and made an *auditor*.”

[Col. 1334A] 198. Adeodatus the bishop said: “This must be preserved for the inquiry. He has acknowledged the truth.”

Then he read: “Verianus, bishop from the White Tower” [Note: [Col. 1334C] From the White Tower. Perhaps Aquae Albae in Mauretania Sitifensis.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Verissimus, bishop of Tacarata.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Servatus, bishop of Ampora.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Martialis, bishop of Vatarba” [Note: [Col. 1334C] Vatarba. Its province is uncertain.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed; I have no opponent.”

Then he read: “Donatus, bishop of Tamascanina” [Note: [Col. 1334C] Tamascanina, or Tamascana. In Mauretania Sitifensis, as the list, no. 34, indicates; the municipality of Tamascani is found in the Peutinger Table.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Quadratianus, bishop of the people of Sicilibba” [Note: [Col. 1334C] Sicilibba. In the proconsular province. For at the Council of Carthage in 449, Praetextatus, bishop of Sicilibba, was present as one of the bishops of the proconsular province. At the Council of Carthage under Cyprian, Satius of Sicilibba delivered an opinion. Antoninus has Sicilibra; [Col. 1334D] the Anonymous Ravennate, Siciliba.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

[Col. 1334B] Then he read: “Saturnus, bishop of Sita” [Note: [Col. 1334D] Sita. In Mauretania Caesariensis, as the list, no. 112, indicates.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Junior, bishop of Rusiccada” [Note: [Col. 1334D] Rusiccada. In Numidia. See note 49 on book I of Optatus.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Miggin, bishop of Edistia” [Note: [Col. 1334D] Edistia. Its province is uncertain.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Fidentius, bishop of Diana” [Note: [Col. 1334D] Diana. In Numidia according to Antoninus’s Itinerary, where there are two places called Diana.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Geminius, bishop of Clypea.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Marcianus, bishop of Assaba.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Rogatianus, bishop from Vicus Ater” [Note: [Col. 1334D] From Vicus Ater. In Byzacena, as the list, no. 92, indicates. At the Council of Carthage in 525, Peter the Abbot, defending his monastery’s immunity, cited the example of the Monastery of Praecisum: although it lay in the middle of the Church of Leptiminus, it passed over the neighboring bishop and received protection from the bishop of the Church of Vicus Ater, who was at a distance. In the synodical letter of the fathers of Byzacena at the Lateran Council under Martin, Ebasius, bishop of the holy Church of Vicus Ater, subscribed.]

When he came forward, [Col. 1335A] he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Donatus, bishop of Bucconia” [Note: [Col. 1335C] Bucconia, or Bocconia, in Numidia, as the list, no. 13, indicates.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed; I have no opponent.”

Then he read: “Donatus, bishop of Tegulata” [Note: [Col. 1335C] Tegulata, or Teglata. In Numidia, as the list, no. 69, indicates.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Donatus, bishop of Zica” [Note: [Col. 1335C] Zica. Perhaps Zigges, listed in the proconsular province, no. 41.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Felix, bishop of Magarmelita.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Marcellinus, bishop of Mullita.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Benenatus, bishop from the Huts of Silvana” [Note: [Col. 1335C] From the Huts of Silvana. Its province is uncertain.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Rufinus, bishop of Labda” [Note: [Col. 1335C] Labda. In the proconsular province, as the list, no. 18, indicates. Victor, bishop of Labda, attended the Synod of Carthage in 525 under Boniface.]

When he came forward, [Col. 1335B] he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Victor, bishop of Dionysiana” [Note: [Col. 1335C] Dionysiana. In the province of Byzacena, as the same list, no. 111, indicates. At the Council of Carthage under Cyprian, Pomponius of Dionysiana delivered an opinion. Fortunatus of Dionysiana subscribed at the Council of Cabarsussus.]

Primianus, bishop of Carthage, said: “He is ill.”

Then he read: “Benenatus, bishop of Mesarfelta” [Note: [Col. 1335D] Mesarfelta. In Byzacena. For Mesarfilia, or Mesarfelta, is located in the Peutinger Table between Zyrna, Masclae, and Gemellae, towns of the province of Byzacena.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed; and I have no opponent.”

Aurelius, bishop of the Catholic Church of Macomadia, said: “You do have one. Your persecution has destroyed very many citizens. Lucianus was bishop there. It still has someone to be ordained.”

Then he read: “Gloriosus, bishop of Migirpa.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Junianus, bishop of Lamigiga.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Paulus, bishop of Sicca.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Felicianus, bishop of [Col. 1335C] Aquae Novae” [Note: [Col. 1335D] Aquae Novae. In Numidia, as the list, no. 73, indicates.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Aemilianus, [Col. 1336A] bishop of Verrona” [Note: [Col. 1335D] Verrona. Its province is uncertain.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Secundinus, bishop of Uvaza.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Bellicius, bishop of Thelepte.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Lucius, bishop of Zaba” [Note: [Col. 1335D] Zaba. There are two Zabæ in the list: one in Numidia, no. 70; the other in Mauretania Sitifensis, no. 40. See what we said in note 39 on book II of Optatus.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Bebianus, bishop of Dusis” [Note: [Col. 1335D] Dusis. Its province is uncertain.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Bonifacius, bishop of Utimma.” When he came forward, 283 he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Restitutus, bishop of Membressa.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Cresconius, bishop of Aquae” [Note: [Col. 1335D] Cresconius, bishop of Aquae. There were several bishops of Aquae in Africa, and several are mentioned in this conference. Mention has already been made in chapter 135 of Helpidius, Catholic bishop of Aquae in Mauretania Caesariensis, [Col. 1336C] and of Reparatus, his opponent. Here Cresconius, Donatist bishop of Aquae, is mentioned—but in Numidia. For Aurelius, bishop of Macomadia, immediately intervenes as though speaking of a church known to him and nearby. A third, Victorinianus, bishop of Aquae, appears below in chapter 208; Asellicus immediately says that he came from the Arzuges. The province of Arzuges bordered Tripolitania.]

When he came forward, [Col. 1336B] he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed; and I have no *traditor* among my people.”

Aurelius, bishop of the Catholic Church of Macomadia, said: “We have a presbyter there. There was also a bishop there, but he has recently died, and no one has yet been ordained in his place.”

Then he read: “Victor, bishop of Curubis” [Note: [Col. 1336C] Curubis. In the list of the proconsular province, no. 36, it is less correctly called Curbitanum. Peregrinus, bishop of the Church of Curubis, attended the Council of Carthage under Boniface in 525. Saint Augustine mentions Curubis in *The City of God*, book XXII, chapter 8. Pliny, Antoninus in his Itinerary, and the Anonymous Ravennate mention Curubis among the cities of Africa; Ptolemy calls it Curobis or Curabis, [Col. 1336D] book IV, chapter 3.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Saturus, bishop of Bizacium.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Florentinus, bishop of Furni” [Note: [Col. 1336D] Furni. In the proconsular province. In Victor of Vita, book I, no. 3, Mansuetus, bishop of Uricita, is said to have been burned at the Furnitan Gate—that is, at the gate of Carthage by which the road led to the city of Furni. Simeon, bishop of the people of Furni, subscribed at the Council of Carthage under Boniface; that Boniface is said to have consecrated a church at Furni in chapter 29 of the Life of St Fulgentius. Geminius of Furni attended the Council of Carthage under Cyprian.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Aemilianus, bishop of the Median Huts.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Victor, bishop of Gatiana” [Note: [Col. 1336D] Gatiana. Near the end of book III of Victor of Vita mention is made of Bonifacius of Gatiana, distinct from Secundinus of Garriana, who is named in the list of bishops of the province of Byzacena, no. 22. The same see was held by Januarius, bishop of the Church of Gattiana, who subscribed to the synodical letter of the fathers of Byzacena, reported at the Lateran Council under Martin.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave [Col. 1336C] instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Luculus, bishop from the Hospitia.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and [Col. 1337A] signed. I have two opponents against me, and they have just ordained one.”

Then he read: “Romanus, bishop of Lesvis” [Note: [Col. 1337C] Lesvis. In Mauretania Sitifensis, list no. 10. Roughly halfway between Saldae and Sitifis, Lesbi is found in Antoninus’s Itinerary, twenty-five Roman miles from Tubusuptus.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Restitutus, bishop of Segermita.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Cresconius, bishop from Horrea Aninicensis” [Note: [Col. 1337D] From Horrea Aninicensis. In Mauretania Sitifensis, the same as the Horrensis of its list, no. 7. Antoninus, in his Itinerary, mentions Horrea Sitifensis between Sitifis and Tubusuptus, eighteen Roman miles from the former.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Faustinus, bishop of Tambaia.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Primilianus, bishop of Lucimagna” [Note: [Col. 1337D] Lucimagna. Its province is uncertain.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed; I have no opponent.”

Then he read: “Maximianus, bishop of Bennefa.”

Primianus, bishop of Carthage, said: “Today he departed from the body.”

Then he read: “Donatus, [Col. 1337B] bishop of Tisida.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Urbanus, bishop of Tala” [Note: [Col. 1337D] Tala. I do not know what place this is, unless perhaps Tabla in Mauretania Caesariensis, list no. 60; the *Notitia Dignitatum* mentions the frontier-district of Tablata.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Innocentius, bishop of Guzabeta” [Note: [Col. 1337D] Guzabeta. Its province is uncertain.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed; I have no opponent.”

Then he read: “Felix, bishop of Zummis.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

Then he read: “Leontius, bishop of Rusticiana” [Note: [Col. 1337D] Rusticiana. In Numidia, list no. 61. The Peutinger Table has Rustici.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed; I have no opponent.”

Terentius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “This man rebaptized people after joining the party of Donatus. He was subsequently rebaptized and was then ordained.”

199. Adeodatus the bishop said: “Keep to matters belonging to the respective sides.” [Col. 1337C]

Then he read: “Evasius, bishop of Girba.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and signed.”

200. Fortunatius, bishop of the Catholic Church of Sicca, said: “Let it be shown how Felix of Zummis, being absent, could have signed.” And in another hand: “I have verified it.”

201. Marcellinus, a man of clarissimus rank, tribune and notary, said: “You see what is being demanded by your party. For the question is, who subscribed to the mandate in the name of this man who appears not to be presently here.”

Bishop Adeodatus said: “Wait; this is what is being asked.” And in another hand: “I, Bishop Adeodatus, have verified it.”

Bishop Optatus said: “Felix of Lambaesis is ill.”

[Note: **[Col. 1337D] Lambiensis.** In Numidia there was the city of Lambaesis, mentioned by ancient writers. I should believe that this man was bishop of that place [Col. 1338C], rather than of Lanvirita, which is no. 19 in the list of Numidian sees.]

[Col. 1338A] Marcellinus, a man of clarissimus rank, tribune and notary, said: “Let the office clearly show to what place Bishop Felix, who subscribed, belonged.”

And he read: “Felix of Zummi.”

Alypius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “Let it be attested that the falsity of the subscription has been detected.” And in another hand: “I have verified it.”

Bishop Adeodatus said: “This is an error, not a falsification.” And in another hand: “I have verified it.”

Alypius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “A great error. He did not know where he was from.” And in another hand: “I have verified it.”

Possidius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “At least let their notary state who subscribed under his name.” As above.

Alypius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “It is enough that we have not passed these matters over.” As above.

Bishop Petilianus said: “A certain Felix of Lambaesis, our colleague, is ill here; but two others also, namely [Col. 1338B] Flavianus and Donatus, are detained there by no slight illness. I believe that this Felix instructed someone to subscribe on his behalf, and an error was made in the name of the see or place. Let them either take this simply, or we relinquish this name.”

[Note: **[Col. 1338D] Flavianus.** Bishop of Pauzera; above, ch. 187.]

[Note: **[Col. 1338D] Donatus.** Bishop of Sucarda; below, ch. 210.]

And in another hand: “I, Bishop Petilianus, have verified it.”

Marcellinus, a man of clarissimus rank, tribune and notary, said: “You have received the statement, which I think can suffice for you. Therefore allow the remaining names to be read.”

And he read: “Januarius, bishop of Tubursicum of the Numidians.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Securus, bishop of the city of Tenita.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I am here; and I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Donatus, 284 bishop of Ara.”

[Note: **[Col. 1338D] Arensis.** The Donatists enumerate two bishops of this place in this Conference: Donatus here, and, below, in ch. 208, Secundus. They appear to be Numidians.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions [Col. 1338C] and subscribed; and I have no *traditores* among my people.”

Likewise he read: “Marinianus, bishop from Oea.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Montanus, bishop from Cemerinianum.”

[Note: **[Col. 1338D] A Cemeriniano.** It is uncertain in which province this place lay.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed; I have no opponent.”

Fortunatus, bishop of the Catholic Church at Constantine, said: “We have a Church there, and the presbyter Terentius.”

Likewise he read: “Donatianus, bishop of Carcabia.”

[Note: **[Col. 1338D] Carcabianensis.** It was in the province of Byzacena, as the list, no. 84, shows. Victorianus, bishop of Carcabia, who attended the Council of Cabarsussa and was deposed from his see at Bagai, is well known.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Justus, bishop of Niciba.”

[Note: **[Col. 1338D] Nicibensis.** Perhaps Niba in Numidia, no. 8 in the list.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Felix, bishop of Tagara.”

[Note: **[Col. 1338D] Tagaraiensis.** Besides Tagarata, a city of the proconsular province, there was a see of Tagariana in Byzacena, as the list, no. 37, shows. Perhaps this is the man who [Col. 1339C], in the letter of the bishops of Byzacena at the Lateran Council under Martin, is called bishop of Tugaza.]

[Col. 1339A] When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Victor, bishop of Equizetum.”

[Note: **[Col. 1339C] Equizetensis, or Eguizotensis.** In Mauretania Sitifensis, no. 11 in the list. The Peutinger Table has Equeheto.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Januarius, bishop of Horrea Caelia.”

[Note: **[Col. 1339C] Horreae Caeliensis.** In Byzacena, as the list, no. 113, shows. Tenax from Horrea Caelia attended the Council of Carthage under St. Cyprian. In the Antonine Itinerary, Horrea Caelia is a village of Byzacena. Hilarinus, bishop of Horrea Caelia, attended the Synod of Carthage under Aurelius in 419, as legate of the province of Byzacena.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Cresconius, bishop of Pudentiana.”

[Note: **[Col. 1339C] Pudentianensis.** In the Numidian list, no. 44, it is Punentiana. Gregory the Great, Letter 33, Book II, indiction 10, mentions Maximianus, bishop of the Church of Pudentiana in Numidia.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed. But I have no *traditores* among my people or in my whole diocese.”

Aurelius, bishop of the Catholic Church at Macomades, said: “We had there a most reverend man, Bishop Memmianus. Later we ordained another Memmianus there. They have died. We are ordaining another.”

Bishop Adeodatus said: “For whom?”

Aurelius, bishop of the Catholic Church at Macomades, said: “Once you have been removed, we shall ordain one. They themselves abandoned [Col. 1339B] the basilicas; they themselves carried off the Church’s furnishings. The man who is speaking abandoned four basilicas in one place.”

Likewise he read: “Januarius, bishop of Aptuca.”

[Note: **[Col. 1339D] Januarius, bishop of Aptuca.** Above, ch. 128. Januarius, bishop of Aptuca, is numbered among the Catholics, being then held back by bodily illness. Now another Januarius, bishop of the same see and of the Donatist faction, appears; but Victor, the Catholic bishop of Libertum, denies that he is a bishop and affirms that unity is there.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Victor, bishop of the Catholic Church at Libertum, said: “Unity is there; the public conscience is not unaware of it.”

Likewise he read: “Fidentius, bishop of Cullita.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Saturninus, bishop of Gazabia.”

[Note: **[Col. 1339D] Gazabianensis.** Perhaps the same man who, in the Numidian list, no. 93, is called bishop of Gaudiaba.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Vitalis, bishop of Masculita.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Aurelius, bishop of the Catholic Church at Macomades, said: “This Vitalis was a Catholic deacon in the city of Sitifis. Having been rebaptized, he was made a presbyter. [Col. 1339C] He was expelled on account of adultery and afterwards made bishop.”

Bishop Petilianus said: “You chose to stand in the position of an accuser.” And in another hand: “I have verified it.”

Aurelius, [Col. 1340A] bishop of the Catholic Church at Macomades, said: “Not in the position of an accuser, but for the purpose of clearing the matter.”

Likewise he read: “Rufinianus, bishop of Tuburbis.” When he came forward, [he said the same]: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Cresconius, bishop of Baiesita.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Saturninus, bishop of Victoriana.”

[Note: **[Col. 1339D] Victorianensis.** In Byzacena, as the list, no. 88, shows. Saturninus of Victoriana attended the Council of Carthage under Cyprian. Augustine praises Restitutus, bishop of Victoriana, in Letter 105. Getulicus, bishop of Victoriana, subscribed among the Donatists at the Council of Cabarsussa.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Lucianus, bishop of Burugia.”

[Note: **[Col. 1339D] Burugiatensis.** At the Council of Carthage under Cyprian, Quietus from Buruch delivered an opinion; this see may perhaps be the same as that one [Col. 1340C]. Learned men judge Buruch to have been in Numidia, as in the list, no. 5.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Maximus, bishop of Abitina.”

[Note: **[Col. 1340C] Abitinensis.** Abitina was a city of the proconsular province; its bishop Augustalis subscribed to the synodal letter of the bishops of that province under Martin. Saturninus of Avitina subscribed at the Council of Carthage under Cyprian. Augustine mentions the same city in Book III against the Letter of Parmenianus and Book IV against Cresconius, ch. 49; the Anonymous of Ravenna has Bithina among the cities of Africa. The martyrs of Abitina are celebrated, and we possess their acts.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Victor, bishop of Gibba.”

[Note: **[Col. 1340C] Gibbensis or Gilbensis.** In Numidia there are two sees of Gilba, one no. 40 and the other no. 90 in the list. [Col. 1340D] This bishop belonged to one or the other. At the Council of Carthage under Cyprian, Lucius of Castrum Galbae delivered an opinion; that place is Castrum Gilba, also called thus by Augustine and Victor of Vita, at the Council of Milevis, and at the Council of Carthage under Boniface.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Victorianus, bishop of Tunusuda.” [Col. 1340B] When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Cresconius, [bishop] of Ausugraba.”

[Note: **[Col. 1340D] Ausugrabensis.** It is uncertain in which province this place lay.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Fortunatianus, bishop from Senemsalis.”

[Note: **[Col. 1340D] A Senemsalis.** In the proconsular province. At the Council of Carthage in 525 under Boniface, Patronianus of Senemsalis is numbered among the proconsular bishops; and in the synodal letter of the bishops of the same province under Martin, Julianus, bishop of the holy Church of the two Senepsalitanae or Senemsalitinae, subscribes. From this, as Baluzius—most sagacious in correcting ancient codices—observed, in the list of the proconsular province, no. 16, *Duassedemsaï* should be read *Duarum-Senemsalium*, “of the two Senemsales.”]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Salustius, bishop of Zerta.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Hilarius, bishop of Sullita.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

“Likewise he read: ‘Victor, bishop of Tabora.’” And when he had read it, Victor, bishop of Tabora, said: “I had indeed received the mandate; but because our most blessed father and chief Primianus has now received it, it is necessary for me to give instructions concerning these proceedings.”

Marcellinus, a man of clarissimus rank, tribune and notary, said: “The proceedings [Col. 1340C] will preserve your intention.”

Likewise he read: “Argutus, bishop of Tabuda.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Felix, bishop of the royal Manazenes [Col. 1341A].”

[Note: **[Col. 1341C] Manazenensium regiorum.** In Mauretania Caesariensis. For in its list, no. 82, appears Manaccenserita.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “285 I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Macrobius, bishop of Hippo.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Maximinus, bishop of Uzabira.”

[Note: **[Col. 1341C] Uzabirensis.** In the province of Byzacena. For in its list, no. 41, Unuzibira occurs; and in the [Col. 1341D] synodal letter of the fathers of Byzacena at the Lateran Council, Donatus, by God’s mercy bishop of the holy Church of Unizivera, subscribes.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Cresconius, bishop of Silemsilis.”

[Note: **[Col. 1341D] Silemsilensis.** At the Council of Carthage in 397 under Genethlius, a bishop of Selemselis was present; that place appears to have been in the proconsular province.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed. I have no *traditores* among my people.”

Aurelius, bishop of the Catholic Church at Macomades, said: “We have a presbyter who ministers there.”

202. Bishop Adeodatus said: “You said, ‘ministers.’ If you wish to scatter your people everywhere, you now seem to have a share with us in those places where there are Christians.” And in another hand: “I have verified it.”

Likewise he read: “Gaudentius, [Col. 1341B] bishop of Nigizuba.”

[Note: **[Col. 1341D] Nigizubitanus.** It is uncertain in which province this place lay.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Cresconius, bishop of Sinita.”

[Note: **[Col. 1341D] Sinitensis.** In Numidia, as the list, no. 67, shows. Near royal Hippo there was a fortress of Sinita, according to Augustine, *City of God*, Book XXII, ch. 8. In Letter 105, no. 4, he also mentions Marcellinus, the Catholic bishop of this place.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Turrasius, bishop of Fissana.”

[Note: **[Col. 1341D] Fissanensis.** Where this place was is uncertain. Donatus, bishop of Fisciana, attended the Council of Cabarsussa.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Speratus, bishop of Cataqua.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Fortunatianus, bishop of Vensana.”

[Note: **[Col. 1341D] Vensanensis.** It is uncertain in which province this place lay.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Januarius, bishop of Centuriona.”

[Note: **[Col. 1341D] Centurionensis.** In Numidia. Nabor of Centuriones was present at the Council of Cirta. This place differs from Centuria, whose Donatist bishop was Cresconius, as is clear from ch. 126 above.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Comparator, bishop of Mactaris.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Cresconius, bishop of Banzara.”

[Note: **[Col. 1342C] Banzarensis.** It is uncertain in which province this place lay.]

[Col. 1341C] When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed; I have no *traditor* among my people.”

Likewise he read: “Victor, bishop of Hilta.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Victor, bishop of Titulita.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Felix, bishop of Voseta.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

203. Palatinus, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “He was a deacon and was rebaptized.”

Bishop Adeodatus said: “Reserve the matters that belong to the parties.” And in another hand: [Col. 1342A] “I, Bishop Adeodatus, have verified it.”

Likewise he read: “Rogatus, bishop of Zaraita.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Cresconius, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “He was a Catholic deacon and was rebaptized.”

Bishop Adeodatus said: “Reserve the matters that belong to the parties.”

Likewise he read: “Maximinus, bishop of Tuburbis.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Donatus, bishop from the Medianae of the Zabunii.”

[Note: **[Col. 1342C] A Medianis Zabuniorum.** In the list of bishops of Byzacena, no. 27, Mediana occurs; [Col. 1342D] and in the list of Mauretania Caesariensis, no. 86, Castrum Mediani. But the Mediana in question here belongs to Mauretania Sitifensis, as is inferred from the following statement of Novatus of Sitifis, who says that he ordained a presbyter there.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

204. Victor, bishop of the Catholic Church, said: “Let him prove that he came to the one house which he claims.”

Novatus, bishop of the Catholic Church at Sitifis, said: “Let it be recorded that Medianae of the Zabunii has a presbyter. He himself now holds the people and the basilica. He holds to unity. There is no [Col. 1342B] Donatist there. Over the body of the Catholic bishop I ordained a presbyter, and, God willing, a bishop will be ordained there. But there is no Donatist bishop in the same place.”

Bishop Adeodatus said: “Against these statements, reserve what is appropriate.” And in another hand: “I, Bishop Adeodatus, have verified it.”

Marcellinus, a man of clarissimus rank, tribune and notary, said: “What belongs to the parties will be preserved.”

Likewise he read: “Felix, bishop of Uzalis.”

[Note: **[Col. 1342D] Uzalensis.** In the proconsular province, no. 7 in the list; its Catholic bishop was Evodius. Mustulus, bishop of Uzalis, subscribed at the Council of Carthage under Boniface. Augustine, *City of God*, Book XXII, ch. 8, testifies that this city was close to the colony of Utica. Pliny, Book V, ch. 4, calls the town of Uzalis Latin.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Servandus, bishop from the Huts of Favens.”

[Note: **[Col. 1342D] A Casis Favensibus.** It is uncertain in which province this place lay.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed. I have no *traditor*.”

Likewise he read: “Felix, bishop of Putium.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

205. Bishop Petilianus said: “Let the mandate be established, [Col. 1342C] not the case, which must be examined afterwards.” And in another hand: “I, Bishop Petilianus, have verified it.”

206. Marcellinus, a man of clarissimus rank, tribune and notary, said: “I have ruled on these points rather often; you think it superfluous to linger over them.” Likewise he read: “Messianus, bishop of Seleucia.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Liberantius, bishop of Tisania.”

[Note: **[Col. 1342D] Tisanianensis.** It is uncertain in which province this place lay.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Cresconius, bishop of Advocata.”

[Note: **[Col. 1342D] Advocatensis.** This town is mentioned in the acts of Honoratus, first published by us above, p. [Col. 1343C] 192, where he is said to have come to Carthage from the town of Advocata. I should judge it to have belonged to the proconsular province.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

[Col. 1343A] Likewise he read: “Donatus, bishop of Scillium.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Urbanus, bishop of Vica.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Victorinus, bishop of Hadrumetum.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Maximus, bishop of Caniana.”

[Note: **[Col. 1343C] Canianensis.** It is uncertain in which province this place lay.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Ampelius, bishop of Neapolis.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Maximus, bishop of Macra.”

[Note: **[Col. 1343D] Macrensis.** In Mauretania Sitifensis, as the list, no. 17, shows. Macri, near Cellae, is located in the Antonine Itinerary. The Peutinger Table has Magri.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Idaxius, bishop of Muzucca.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Restitutus, bishop of Flumenpiscum.” When he [Col. 1343B] came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Tertullus, bishop of Ciliba.”

[Note: **[Col. 1343D] Cilibiensis.** In the proconsular province, as appears from the letter of the bishops of that province at the Lateran Council under Martin, to which John of Eliba subscribes. At the Council of Carthage in 525 under Boniface, Restitutus, bishop of the people of Ciliba, subscribes.]

When he came forward, 286 he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

“Likewise he read: ‘Januarius, bishop of Nara.’”

[Note: **[Col. 1343D] Narensis.** In the province of Byzacena, no. 11 in the list; Antoninus mentions Nara in the *Itinerary*.]

When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Honoratus, bishop of Thusdrus.” When he came forward, he said the same: “I gave instructions and subscribed.”

Likewise he read: “Crescentilianus, bishop of Lambiris.”
